strings.{actor} 顺着屋顶爬过去，从二楼的窗户里接出了一对老夫妻，背着他们蹚回了石: {actor} crawls over the rooftops, gets an old couple out through a second-floor window and carries them back through the water to the steps, one after the other.
strings.{name.p3} 犹豫了一下，掰了半块巧克力塞进 {actor} 手里，压低声: {name.p3} hesitates, then breaks off half the chocolate, presses it into {actor}’s hand and whispers, “Don’t tell anyone.”
strings.{protagonist} 喝了一夜的水，熬了过来。: {protagonist} drinks water all night long and pulls through.
strings.{protagonist} 的小腿被倒下的墙压在了山脚的瓦砾里，已经压了几个钟头: {protagonist}’s calf is pinned under a fallen wall in the rubble at the foot of the hill. It has been several hours, and the foot has gone purple and numb. The rescue course covered this: the longer someone is pinned, the more dangerous the moment the weight comes off. But no one can say when the rescue team will get here.
strings.{protagonist} 被抬上山以后，一开始还能说笑。几个钟头后，心口突然一: Once carried up the hill, {protagonist} can still talk and joke at first. A few hours later come sudden bouts of palpitations, numbness in the hands and feet, and urine the colour of soy sauce—crush syndrome has set in.
strings.“……小野寺由美，三十六岁。”葵一下子站了起来，又坐下，把脸埋进了书包里。: “…Onodera Yumi, thirty-six.” Aoi jumps to her feet, sits back down and buries her face in her school bag.
strings.“葵——小野寺葵——”喊声在瓦砾之间来回地响。最后是一个镇民在半塌的公交车站找到: “Aoi! Onodera Aoi!” The calls echo back and forth through the rubble. In the end it is one of the townspeople who finds her, in a half-collapsed bus shelter.
strings.てんでんこ——各自跑。活下来的人，不许怪自己。: Tendenko—everyone runs on their own. And whoever lives is not allowed to blame themselves.
strings.一个中年男人顺着绳子蹚了过来，冻得说不出话。: A middle-aged man wades over along the rope, too frozen to speak.
strings.一个抱着孩子的年轻母亲走到屋檐下，小声问：你们那边还有没有吃的？孩子从昨天到现在: A young mother with a child in her arms comes over to the eaves and asks quietly if you have any food left. Since yesterday her child has eaten half a biscuit, nothing more. Behind her, a few old people are looking this way too.
strings.一个本来就虚弱的老人拉了两天，没能熬过去。: One of the old people, frail to begin with, has diarrhoea for two days and doesn’t pull through.
strings.一个泡了水的急救包，纱布还能用: A waterlogged first-aid kit, the gauze still usable
strings.一个穿着渔协外套的中年人拦住了刚从山下回来的 {actor}，盯着 {actor: A middle-aged man in a fishing co-op jacket steps in front of {actor}, who has just come back up from below, and stares at the bag of biscuits in {actor.his} hand. “That’s from my convenience store.” Behind him stand his wife and two children, grey-faced with hunger.
strings.一个老太太跟着下去看了一眼，在瓦砾上坐了很久。那是她的丈夫。: An old woman goes down to look and sits on the rubble for a long time. It is her husband.
strings.一个背着红书包的小女孩攥住了你们的衣角，一直没有松手——她叫小野寺葵，三年级。: A little girl with a red school bag grabs the hem of your coat and won’t let go—her name is Onodera Aoi, third grade.
strings.一件挂在树杈上的羽绒服，拧干了当场穿上: A down jacket caught in a tree, wrung out and put on on the spot
strings.一具被淤泥盖住的遗体，只好扯下旁边的窗帘盖在上面: A body under a layer of sludge; there was nothing to do but pull down a curtain and cover it
strings.一包没拆封的五号电池: An unopened pack of AA batteries
strings.一回合 = 6 小时，第一回合就是地震和海啸。浪在三四十分钟后到达，第一次预报只: One round is 6 hours, and the first round is the earthquake and the tsunami. The wave arrives thirty to forty minutes later and the first forecast says only three metres; the earlier you run and the higher you go, the more people live. A tsunami is not a single wave: on the first day the later waves can be bigger than the first, and anyone who goes back down to low ground is in the most danger.
strings.一条十几米宽的黄土带横在了山腰上，砍下来的灌木全拖到了下面。渡边老人用脚踩了踩：: A band of bare yellow earth more than ten metres wide now crosses the hillside, the cut brush all dragged down below it. Watanabe presses the ground with his foot. “Like this. The fire won’t get across.”
strings.一来一回要大半天，路上要穿过瓦砾区: There and back takes most of a day, through the rubble
strings.一根锈钉子扎穿了鞋底: A rusty nail went straight through a shoe sole
strings.一箱一箱的罐头被传上了石阶。镇民们排着队领，有个老太太抱着两罐秋刀鱼，对孙丽娜鞠: Case after case of cans is passed up the stone steps. The townspeople line up for their share; one old woman, clutching two cans of saury, bows to Lina Sun again and again.
strings.一箱没开封的两升装矿泉水: An unopened case of two-litre water bottles
strings.一箱泡过水的方便面，袋子都没破: A case of instant noodles, soaked but with every packet intact
strings.一辆一辆卡车载着人，沿着刚推出来的路，慢慢开出了潮见町。: One truck after another, loaded with people, crawls out of Shiomi along the newly cleared road.
strings.一辆挂着“中国驻新潟总领事馆”牌子的大巴停在了山下的路口。一个说中文的年轻人拿着: A bus with a sign reading “Chinese Consulate-General in Niigata” pulls up at the junction below the hill. A young man with a list calls out in Chinese: “Shiomi Fisheries interns! Twenty of you, not one left behind—and we’ve got three seats to spare.” Lina Sun turns to look at you, then at the old people lying on the hill.
strings.一辆翻倒的小货车上拆下来的电瓶: A battery taken out of an overturned pickup truck
strings.一阵剧烈的余震，紧接着，海边的警报器又响了。山上的镇民一下子乱了，有人哭喊着往后: A violent aftershock, and right after it the siren by the sea goes off again. Panic sweeps the townspeople on the hill: some run crying into the woods behind the hill, others fall on the stone steps.
strings.万一火上来，能少死人；可今晚所有人都得在露天里过: If the fire comes, fewer will die; but everyone spends tonight in the open
strings.万一火上来，能少死人；可今晚所有人都要在露天里过: If the fire comes up, fewer will die; but everyone spends tonight in the open
strings.三个白色的大字母躺在神社前的空地上，每一个都有两层楼那么高。: Three huge white letters lie on the open ground in front of the shrine, each as tall as a two-story house.
strings.三月，一个星期五的下午。三陆海岸的潮见町，一座只有一条商店街和一个渔港的小城。你: March, a Friday afternoon. Shiomi is a little town on the Sanriku coast with one shopping street and one fishing harbour. The five of you are trainees on an international disaster-response course, and three months of training come down to one last thing: the final assessment at the Shiomi Fisheries and Disaster Training Centre by the sea.
strings.三陆口音，句子短，像北方的老渔民：“跑。别回头。”“海不骗人。”: A Sanriku accent and short sentences, like an old fisherman anywhere: “Run. Don’t look back.” “The sea doesn’t lie.”
strings.上山，带上走不动的人：抬着千代奶奶的轮椅，一路拍门喊人: Head for the hill, but take those who can’t walk: carry Granny Chiyo’s wheelchair and bang on doors on the way
strings.下山的人在港口边的瓦砾里认出了渡边老人的雨衣。: People who went down find Watanabe’s raincoat in the rubble by the harbour.
strings.下山的人能早一点知道；可冲下去的人，自己也在低处: The people below hear sooner; but whoever runs down is on low ground too
strings.下山远征：去镇公所和诊所: Expedition: the town hall and the clinic
strings.下面太危险；可拦下他，他会恨你们一辈子: It’s too dangerous down there; but if you stop him, he will hate you for the rest of his life
strings.不争辩，用干活说话；要多花些力气去安排: Don’t argue; let the work speak, though it takes more effort to organize
strings.不会说话。低吼、呜咽，偶尔冲着瓦砾叫两声。: Doesn’t talk. Growls, whimpers, now and then barks twice at the rubble.
strings.不冒险；火点会不会连成一片，看运气: No risk; whether the spot fires join up is down to luck
strings.不挪动、不折腾；能不能熬过去，只能看他自己: Don’t move him, don’t fuss; whether he makes it is up to him
strings.不挪动、不折腾；能不能熬过去，看 {protagonist} 自己: No moving, no fuss; pulling through is up to {protagonist} alone
strings.不撒谎，也不说: No lie, but no answer either
strings.不撬：给 {protagonist} 盖上毯子，轮流守着，等救援队带输液来: Don’t pry: cover {protagonist} with a blanket, take turns keeping watch and wait for rescuers to bring an IV drip
strings.不用下到火边；能拖慢火，挡不住火: No need to go down near the fire; it can slow the fire, not stop it
strings.不用下水；可他们得自己蹚过来: No one goes into the water, but they’ll have to wade over on their own
strings.不用再搭上一个人；可隔着两公里，他们未必听得见: No one else has to be put at risk; but two kilometres off, they may not hear it
strings.不用再等了；可抬着担架在雪地里走一整天，会有人倒下: No more waiting; but a whole day of carrying stretchers through the snow, and someone will fall
strings.不费柴；能挡住一部分: No firewood needed; it stops some of it
strings.不走：抬着担架在雪地里走十八公里，会死人的: Don’t go: eighteen kilometres through the snow with stretchers will kill people
strings.东北口音，夹着几个日语词：“没事儿，大丈夫。”“咱先把火整起来。”: A northeastern Chinese accent sprinkled with Japanese: “It’s fine, daijobu.” “Let’s get the fire going first.”
strings.东西救人，就不算偷: If it saves lives, it isn’t stealing
strings.东西本来就是他的: It was his to begin with
strings.两个人一前一后抬起轮椅往石阶上冲，其他人沿着巷子一路拍门、喊人。最后十几级台阶，: Two people lift the wheelchair, one at each end, and charge up the steps while the others run down the alleys banging on doors and shouting. On the last dozen steps, the roar of water is right behind them.
strings.两个人一左一右抱着她，用体温给她暖: Hold her between two of you and warm her with your bodies
strings.两个人在黑暗里转了大半夜，找不到渡边家在哪里，天亮前才互相搀着爬回来。: The two of them stumble through the dark for most of the night and never find where the Watanabe house stood. Just before dawn they climb back up, leaning on each other.
strings.两个人比一个人安全；可山上会少一个干活的人，陪她的人也要在山里过两夜: Two are safer than one; but the hill loses a pair of hands, and whoever goes spends two nights in the mountains
strings.两个人背着水和手电，沿着雪地上的记号走进了林子。: The two of them, with water and flashlights, follow the marks in the snow into the woods.
strings.两个人走得快；投这个选项的人去，要在山里过一夜: Two travel fast; whoever votes for this goes, and spends a night in the mountains
strings.两天的山路，雪还没化，余震不断；她十七岁: Two days of mountain trails, snow still on the ground, aftershocks without end; she’s seventeen
strings.两条皮带勒进了阿部的大腿。房梁撬开的时候，他咬着一块毛巾，一声没吭。: The two belts bite into Abe’s thighs. When the beam comes up, he bites down on a towel and doesn’t make a sound.
strings.两点四十六分，考核进行到第二项。这一次，没有人会喊“推演结束”。: At 2:46 p.m., the assessment reaches its second part. This time, no one is going to call “end of simulation.”
strings.中年人想了想，点点头，抱起小的那个孩子，跟着 {actor} 上了山。: The man thinks it over, nods, picks up the younger child and follows {actor} up the hill.
strings.中年人接过袋子，愣了一下，又从里面掏出两包塞回给 {actor}：“你们也没吃吧: The man takes the bag and hesitates, then pulls out two packets and presses them back into {actor}’s hands. “You haven’t eaten either, have you?”
strings.中年人没再说话，拉着孩子走开了。那以后，屋檐下这边，再没有镇民过来坐。: The man says nothing more and leads his children away. From then on, none of the townspeople come to sit with you under the eaves.
strings.也许只有这一次机会: This may be the only chance
strings.也许是好消息，也许名单念完了也没有那个名字: Maybe good news; maybe the list ends without that name
strings.也许有人在找他: Someone may be looking for him
strings.也许能找到人；也许只能找到房子原来的位置: You might find people; you might find only where the house used to be
strings.也许过两天就好了: Maybe it will pass in a couple of days
strings.也许过两天就没人说了: Maybe in a couple of days no one will be saying it
strings.书包里有我的作业本，明天要交的。: My homework’s in my bag. It’s due tomorrow.
strings.二十个姑娘终于能回家了；山上会少一个翻译、一双手: Twenty young women finally get to go home; the hill loses an interpreter and a pair of hands
strings.二楼的窗外，浪不是一堵墙，是整片海抬了起来。不到一分钟，水就漫过了二楼的天花板。: Outside the second-floor windows, the wave isn’t a wall—the whole sea rises. In less than a minute, the water is over the second-floor ceiling.
strings.人多找得快；可所有人都会散在瓦砾里: More people search faster; but everyone ends up scattered across the rubble
strings.什么也不做，就什么也不会搭进去: Do nothing, and nothing more is lost
strings.什么也改变不了，可他需要有人听: It won’t change anything, but he needs someone to listen
strings.今天下午在研修中心的还有：来讲“渔民的海啸经验”的老渔民渡边正雄和他的柴犬小太郎: Also at the centre this afternoon: Watanabe Masao, an old fisherman invited to talk about “a fisherman’s experience of tsunamis,” and his shiba inu Kotaro; Suzuki Chiyo, an elderly woman in a wheelchair from the nursing home next door, here for a joint drill; Takahashi Misaki, a high school student volunteering for the day; and Lina Sun, a Chinese technical intern borrowed from the fish-processing plant next door to interpret for the assessment.
strings.从今天起，我们的吃的和水跟镇民一起分: From today, we share our food and water with the townspeople
strings.从山顶回头看，黑色的水墙越过了防波堤，研修中心、养老院和半条商店街一起被推着往镇: Looking back from the top of the hill, a black wall of water rolls over the breakwater, carrying the training centre, the nursing home and half the shopping street into the town.
strings.从瓦砾里捡来的木头：房梁、门板、渔箱，到处都是，可大多泡过海水，还带着钉子。生火: Wood picked out of the rubble: beams, doors, fish crates. It is everywhere, but most of it is soaked in seawater and studded with nails. You need it for the fire and for melting snow.
strings.从石阶上扔绳子，喊他们自己顺着绳子过来: Throw a rope from the steps and shout for them to come over along it
strings.仓库后面堆着的旧木板和祭礼用的木架: Old boards and festival frames stacked behind the shed
strings.仓库最里面翻出了一台煤油暖炉，油箱里还有半箱油。仓库里挤满了人，门窗都关着。: Someone digs a kerosene heater out of the very back of the shed, its tank still half full. The shed is packed with people, the door and windows shut.
strings.仓库的另一头用纸箱隔了出来。新的厕所坑挖在了下风口。: The far end of the shed is screened off with cardboard boxes. The new latrine pit goes in downwind.
strings.仓库角落里那箱运动服大小都不合身。湿衣服挂在屋檐下，不一会儿就冻成了硬板。: None of the tracksuits in the shed’s box fit anyone. The wet clothes hung under the eaves freeze into boards in no time.
strings.仓库里分到的几瓶两升装矿泉水。山上的人很多，水是按人头分的。: A few two-litre bottles of water from the shed. There are a lot of people on the hill, and the water is shared out by head.
strings.他们刚搬出几箱，冷库后面的油罐“轰”地喷出一团火。{actor} 的胳膊被燎了一: They have only got a few cases out when the oil tank behind the cold store goes up with a roar, belching a ball of fire. {actor}’s arm gets singed, and everyone drops the rest of the cases and runs.
strings.他们在瓦砾里转了一个下午，连佐佐木家原来在哪条街都认不出来了。: They spend the whole afternoon wandering the rubble and can’t even tell which street the Sasaki house was on.
strings.他们带着输液和液压顶杆，能先输液、再解压: They have IV drips and a hydraulic jack: fluids first, then the weight comes off
strings.他们手里有各个避难所的名单，可要等消息回来: They have every shelter’s list, but word will take time to come back
strings.他们找到了佐佐木家的地基，房子不在了。孙丽娜在一堆瓦砾里捡起一只小女孩的拖鞋，放: They find the foundations of the Sasaki house. The house is gone. From a heap of rubble Lina Sun picks up a little girl’s slipper and puts it in her pocket.
strings.他们找到了渡边家的地基。房子不在了，只剩一块门牌。老人把门牌揣进怀里，跟着 {a: They find the foundations of the Watanabe house. The house itself is gone; only the nameplate is left. The old man tucks it inside his coat and follows {actor} back.
strings.他们最怕冷: They feel the cold the most
strings.他们最熬不住冷；你们自己再等一等: They’re the least able to take the cold; you can hold out a little longer
strings.伤口感染比冷更要命: An infected wound is deadlier than the cold
strings.伤得最重、病得最重的人先走——不管是谁: The worst injured and the sickest go first—whoever they are
strings.低处镇区的水深。海啸过后会慢慢退去，可地面沉降了，涨潮时低处还会进水。: How deep the water is in the low part of town. It drains away slowly after the tsunami, but the ground has sunk, and the lowest streets flood again at high tide.
strings.余震中被瓦砾压住: Pinned under rubble in an aftershock
strings.余震中被瓦砾砸中: Struck by rubble in an aftershock
strings.余震按大森公式衰减：每 6 小时发生有感余震的概率约为 8 ÷（震后小时数 +: Aftershocks decay according to Omori’s law: the chance of a felt aftershock in any 6 hours is about 8 ÷ (hours since the quake + 10)—better than even on the first night, under one in ten by the fourth day. About three in ten are strong ones that can injure people working in the rubble and may bring a tsunami warning. The fire in town spreads at night, faster in the wind, and rain or snow damp it down; once it gets into the cedar woods on the slope it heads straight for the hilltop, and a firebreak is the only thing that can stop it.
strings.你们也要活下去: You have to stay alive too
strings.你们也要活命；可山上的人都看着: You have to live too, but everyone on the hill is watching
strings.你们分头冲进水产厂和养老院，一路喊着“海啸！上山！”。十几分钟后，黑色的水墙越过: You split up and dash into the fish plant and the nursing home, shouting “Tsunami! Up the hill!” all the way. Ten-odd minutes later, a black wall of water rolls over the breakwater.
strings.你们分成两组，一组沿着山脚往东，一组往港口。镇民里有人追上来，报着亲人的名字。: You split into two groups, one along the foot of the hill to the east, one toward the harbour. Townspeople run after you, calling out the names of their families.
strings.你们在瓦砾上插了一根挂着红布的竹竿，把一瓶水和一条毯子塞进了缝里。阿部在下面喊：: You plant a bamboo pole with a red rag on the rubble and push a bottle of water and a blanket into the gap. Abe calls up from below, “Come back tomorrow!”
strings.你们挤进了社务所，背靠着墙坐下。门口那几位被挤出去的老人裹着纸箱板，一直没有说话: You squeeze into the shrine office and sit with your backs to the wall. The old people pushed out to the doorway wrap themselves in cardboard and say nothing.
strings.你们是从中国来的吗？我会说“你好”。: Are you from China? I can say “ni hao.”
strings.你们是外地人，本来就不该在这里；可山上的老人会看着你们上车: You’re outsiders and were never meant to be here; but the old people on the hill will watch you board
strings.你们站在神社前回头看：黑色的水墙越过了防波堤，推着房子、渔船和汽车往镇子里涌。研: You stand in front of the shrine and look back: a black wall of water rolls over the breakwater and drives houses, boats and cars into the town. Of the training centre’s second floor, only the roof is left.
strings.你们跟在自卫队员后面，又一次下到了瓦砾里。: You follow the troops down into the rubble once again.
strings.你们跟着一百多个人挤上了小学的楼顶。浪来的时候，黑水漫过了楼顶的栏杆，一直淹到胸: You crowd onto the school roof with more than a hundred others. When the wave comes, black water pours over the roof railings and rises to your chests.
strings.你吃上一口，替 {name.p3} 保密: You get a bite and keep {name.p3}’s secret
strings.便利店废墟里的几包饼干和泡了水的饭团: A few packets of biscuits and soggy rice balls from the ruined convenience store
strings.便利店的卷帘门被冲歪了，货架倒了一地。有人捡起一袋饼干，犹豫了一下，还是塞进了包: The convenience store’s shutter has been bent askew and the shelves lie scattered on the floor. Someone picks up a bag of biscuits, hesitates, and puts it in a bag anyway.
strings.修好摔坏的电台和天线，就能和町灾害对策本部说上话。光修好还不够，还要一块汽车电瓶: Fix the broken radio and its antenna and you can talk to the town disaster headquarters. Repairing it isn’t enough, though: you also need a car battery to power it.
strings.傍晚，后面的浪一波接一波地涌上来，有一波比第一波还高，一直冲到了石阶的第十几级。: In the evening the later waves surge in one after another, one of them higher than the first, reaching the tenth step and beyond.
strings.傍晚，消息传了回来：小野寺由美，在内陆中学的避难所，冻伤了脚，活着。: Toward evening the word comes back: Onodera Yumi, at the shelter in the inland junior high. Frostbitten feet. Alive.
strings.先做好转移的准备：把老人、伤员和物资挪到神社后面的背风坡: Get ready to move: carry the old, the injured and the supplies to the lee slope behind the shrine
strings.先别慌：用电池多听一会儿广播，弄清楚有多远、风往哪边吹（用掉 1 节电池）: Don’t panic yet: listen to the radio a while longer and find out how far it is and which way the wind blows (uses 1 AA battery)
strings.先去救山脚下还压着的阿部: First go and free Abe, still pinned at the foot of the hill
strings.先去瓦砾里找吃的喝的：便利店、自动售货机、水产厂的冷库: Look for food and water in the rubble first: the convenience store, the vending machines, the fish plant’s cold store
strings.先去隔壁喊人：水产厂里有二十个实习生，养老院里还有走不动的老人: Go next door and raise the alarm first: twenty interns in the fish plant, old people in the nursing home who can’t walk
strings.先在山顶摆出 SOS，点起烟，让直升机看见我们: Lay out an SOS on the hilltop and make smoke so the helicopters see us
strings.先多喝点水，再让大家撬（用掉 2 升水）: Drink plenty of water first, then let them pry (uses 2 L of water)
strings.先把伤得最重的人抬下山，送去直升机降落场: Carry the worst injured down to the helicopter landing site first
strings.先把山上的人组织起来：登记名字、分组、定好规矩: Organize the people on the hill first: register names, form groups, set some rules
strings.先把老人、伤员和物资转移到后山的背风坡: Move the old, the injured and the supplies to the lee slope behind the hill first
strings.先抢出水和吃的，再撤: Save the water and food first, then go
strings.先照顾山上的老人和孩子: Look after the old people and children on the hill first
strings.先用皮带勒紧他的两条大腿，再撬: Strap his thighs tight with belts first, then pry
strings.先给他喂温水、盖上毯子，再一点一点撬（用掉 2 升水）: Give him warm water and a blanket first, then pry a little at a time (uses 2 L of water)
strings.先补水再解压: Fluids first, then take the weight off
strings.先补水再解压，是救援课上教过的；要多花几个钟头，水也要从大家嘴里省出来: Fluids before releasing the weight—that’s what the rescue course taught; it takes hours longer, and the water has to come out of everyone’s mouths
strings.先补水再解压，风险小得多；要用掉两升水: Fluids before releasing the weight—far less risky; it takes two litres of water
strings.先让 {protagonist} 喝下两升水，再撬: Get two litres of water into {protagonist} first, then pry
strings.先让一个大人单独听，是好消息再告诉她（用掉 1 节电池）: Have one adult listen alone first, and tell her only if it’s good news (uses 1 AA battery)
strings.先让他喝下两升温水，再撬: Have him drink two litres of warm water first, then pry
strings.先问老板：能不能拿: Ask the owner first: can we take them?
strings.全体马上撤：翻山往内陆走，老人和伤员用担架抬: Everyone leaves now: over the mountains inland, carrying the old and the injured on stretchers
strings.内向、谨慎，什么事都先算一遍再动手；对机器比对人有耐心。害怕的时候，话会变得特别: Introverted and careful; he works everything out before he acts and has more patience with machines than with people. When he’s scared, he talks a lot.
strings.内陆中学的体育馆里挤满了人。一个脚上缠着绷带的女人从人群里挤出来，一瘸一拐地跑过: The gym of the inland junior high was packed. A woman with a bandaged foot pushed out of the crowd and ran, limping, to throw her arms around the little girl with the red school bag. The girl didn’t cry; she just held on to the hem of her mother’s jacket. Those who lived: {survivors}. Those who never made it down from the hill: {dead}. Later, many people who talked about those days began with this moment.
strings.再也没有人会看到: No one will ever see it
strings.再等两天：等自卫队来了，跟着他们的车绕过去: Wait two more days: when the Self-Defense Forces come, go round with their trucks
strings.冷库里有好几千罐秋刀鱼罐头。都是我们切的。: There are thousands of cans of saury in the cold store. We cut every one of those fish.
strings.冷静、利落，看人先看伤，说话不绕弯子。心里那根弦一直绷着，不肯承认自己也会怕；最: Calm and brisk; she looks at the injury before the person and never beats around the bush. The string inside her is always taut, and she won’t admit she can be afraid; what she can least bear is being unable to do anything.
strings.冷？不冷。我年轻的时候，大雪天走两个钟头山路去接生。: Cold? Not me. When I was young I walked two hours over the mountain in heavy snow to deliver a baby.
strings.几个人喊着号子把房梁撬起了一指宽，七手八脚把阿部拖了出来。: Chanting the count, you lever the beam up a finger’s width and drag Abe out with a tangle of hands.
strings.几个人带着撬棍下了石阶。: A few people go down the stone steps with crowbars.
strings.几个人带着撬棍和千斤顶下了山。: A few of you go down the hill with crowbars and a jack.
strings.几个人把撬棍塞进房梁底下，喊着号子往下压。: A few of you jam crowbars under the beam and heave down on them, chanting the count.
strings.几个人把撬棍插进墙底下，喊着号子往下压。: A few people jam crowbars under the wall and heave down on a shouted count.
strings.几个人跟着小太郎下了石阶。: A few people follow Kotaro down the stone steps.
strings.几个人顶着湿毯子冲进了着火的仓库。: A few people throw wet blankets over their heads and rush into the burning shed.
strings.几分钟后，海边那个还能响的警报器拉响了海啸警报。山上的人全都站了起来，往海的方向: A few minutes later the one siren by the sea that still works starts wailing a tsunami warning. Everyone on the hill gets to their feet and looks toward the sea.
strings.几十个人乱成一团，什么也干不成；可这要有人站出来，让人服气: Dozens of people in chaos get nothing done; but it takes someone to stand up whom people will listen to
strings.几十个人互相搀着，沿着后山的小路又往上爬了一百多米。警报解除的时候，已经过去了好: Holding each other up, dozens of people climb another hundred-odd metres up the path behind the hill. By the time the warning is lifted, hours have passed.
strings.几十个人排成一条长龙，一桶一桶地往屋檐和地上泼雪水。: Dozens of people form a long chain, sloshing bucket after bucket of snowmelt onto the eaves and the ground.
strings.几十个人排成长龙，把雪一桶一桶地泼到屋顶上。: Dozens of people form a long chain, throwing snow onto the roofs one bucket at a time.
strings.几十个人等着这一格信号: Dozens of people are waiting for this one bar
strings.几十个镇民里，有好几个已经熬不住了: Of the dozens of townspeople, several can’t hold out much longer
strings.删掉它：那一分钟不该存在: Delete it: that minute should never have existed
strings.别理：越解释越说不清: Ignore it: the more you explain, the murkier it gets
strings.到山脚的瓦砾堆里拣木头：房梁、门板、渔箱，到处都是，可大多泡过海水，还带着钉子，: Pick wood out of the rubble at the foot of the hill: beams, doors and fish crates are everywhere, but most of it is soaked in seawater and full of nails, and the wet wood has to be dragged up thirty metres of stone steps. The foot of the hill is where the tsunami came through—on the first day more waves can come at any time, and later the strong aftershocks may bring tsunami warnings.
strings.到瓦砾里翻找能用的东西：便利店、自动售货机、倒塌的民房、诊所和药店。吃的、喝的、: Search the rubble for anything useful: the convenience store, vending machines, collapsed houses, the clinic and the pharmacy. There may be food, drink, medicine and batteries—or a rusty nail through your foot, or a body. All of these things belonged to someone.
strings.剩下的座位，给了镇上病得最重的几个老人。: The remaining seats go to the sickest of the town’s old people.
strings.劈了参道旁的两条长凳: Split the two benches along the shrine approach
strings.勒了止血带，房梁也撬开了，阿部还是没有挺过来。: Tourniquets on, beam pried up, and still Abe doesn’t make it.
strings.十几个穿迷彩服的自卫队员背着大包，踩着瓦砾爬上了石阶。带队的人喘着气说：“这一带: A dozen or so SDF troops in camouflage, big packs on their backs, pick their way over the rubble and up the stone steps. Their leader says between breaths, “The roads around here are still cut. We walked over from the other side of the mountains.” They have brought water, rice balls, blankets, a medical kit and a satellite phone.
strings.十几支手电散开在山脚下的瓦砾里。: More than a dozen flashlights fan out across the rubble at the foot of the hill.
strings.千代奶奶住进了内陆的一家养老院，离潮见四十公里。床头放着一张潮见港的老照片。来看: Granny Chiyo went into a nursing home inland, forty kilometres from Shiomi, with an old photo of Shiomi harbour by her bed. She had many visitors, most of them babies she had delivered, some of them grandfathers by then. She died in the winter of her ninety-first year, saying to the end, “Chiba, that girl—she pushed me so steady.”
strings.千代奶奶拉住 {actor} 的袖子：“孩子，你是点名的那个吧？千叶呢？她推我上: Granny Chiyo catches {actor}’s sleeve. “Child, you’re the one who did the head count, aren’t you? Where’s Chiba? She pushed me up here and then ran back… When you counted, was she there?”
strings.千代奶奶是被两个消防团员连人带轮椅从水里拖上来的，浑身湿透，嘴唇发紫，一直在咳。: Granny Chiyo is dragged out of the water, wheelchair and all, by two volunteer firefighters, soaked through, lips blue, coughing and coughing.
strings.千代奶奶松开了手，看着雪看了很久：“那孩子就是那样的人。……不怪你，孩子。不怪你: Granny Chiyo lets go and watches the snow for a long time. “That’s just how that girl is. …It’s not your fault, child. Not your fault.”
strings.千代奶奶没能走下那座山。{actor} 后来找到了千叶的父母，把那天的事从头讲了: Granny Chiyo never made it down from that hill. {actor} later found Chiba’s parents and told them the whole story of that day, including the “Everyone’s here.” When {actor} finished, Chiba’s mother got up and poured {actor.him} a cup of tea.
strings.千代奶奶没能走下那座山。养老院的人后来在她轮椅的坐垫底下找到一个布包，里面是一叠: Granny Chiyo never made it down from the hill. Later, the nursing-home staff found a cloth bundle under the cushion of her wheelchair: a stack of birth records, the earliest page from 1951, written in a neat, careful hand. The records went to Shiomi’s earthquake archive.
strings.千代奶奶点点头：“那就好，小学结实。”{actor} 没敢看她的眼睛。: Granny Chiyo nods. “Good. That school is sturdy.” {actor} can’t bring {actor.himself} to look her in the eye.
strings.千代奶奶的轮椅卡在了石阶下面。美咲回头去拉，被渡边老人一把拽住。水墙过去以后，石: Granny Chiyo’s wheelchair is stuck at the bottom of the steps. Misaki turns back to pull it and Watanabe grabs her and hauls her away. When the wall of water has passed, there is nothing at the bottom of the steps.
strings.千代奶奶看了 {actor} 一会儿，没再问。: Granny Chiyo looks at {actor} for a while and asks nothing more.
strings.千代奶奶缩在毯子里，哼了一声，又没了动静。: Granny Chiyo curls up in her blanket, murmurs once, and goes still again.
strings.千代奶奶被抬上了大巴，躺在最后一排。: Granny Chiyo is carried onto the bus and laid across the back row.
strings.千代奶奶被裹进保温毯，抬下了山。: Granny Chiyo is wrapped in a thermal blanket and carried down the hill.
strings.千代奶奶，我给您把毯子掖好。: Granny Chiyo, let me tuck your blanket in.
strings.千叶那孩子……推我上来以后又跑回去了。她才二十三岁。: Chiba, that girl… she pushed me up here and then ran back. She’s only twenty-three.
strings.半个月后，研修班的事务局在遇难者名单里找到了五个学员的名字。八幡神社的山坡上，雪: Two weeks later, the course office found the names of all five trainees on the list of the dead. On the slopes of the Hachiman Shrine, the snow melted and fell again. Those on the hill who survived: {survivors}. Afterwards they seldom spoke of the trainees from far away; they remembered only their accents, and the eaves where they had spent their last days. The next year the course went ahead as usual. In the first lesson, the instructor wrote a single line on the blackboard: “When the sea pulls back, run.”
strings.半堵泡软了的墙倒了下来，{actor} 的小腿被压在了下面，怎么也抽不出来。: Half a sodden wall topples over and traps {actor}’s calf; it won’t come free.
strings.半堵泡软了的墙倒了下来，正好压在 {actor} 身上。旁边的人扒了很久，才把: Half a sodden wall topples over and lands right on {actor}. It takes the people nearby a long time to dig {actor.him} out.
strings.半夜，{protagonist} 说了句“有点困”，就再也没有醒过来。: In the middle of the night, {protagonist} says, “I’m a bit sleepy,” and never wakes up.
strings.半夜，渡边老人披上一件捡来的雨衣，拄着一根竹竿往石阶下面走，小太郎跟在他脚边。有: In the middle of the night, Watanabe throws on a raincoat he has scavenged and starts down the stone steps leaning on a bamboo pole, Kotaro at his heels. Someone grabs him and he shakes the hand off. “My old woman has bad legs. She can’t run fast. I have to go and look.” Below the hill is all rubble, the fire is still burning, and the aftershocks keep coming.
strings.半夜，阿部说了句“有点困”，就再也没有醒过来。: In the middle of the night Abe says, “Bit sleepy,” and never wakes up.
strings.厂长说，你们先上去，别等我。……他到现在还没上来。: The manager said, “You go on up, don’t wait for me.” …He still hasn’t come up.
strings.压了才几个钟头，挤压综合征的风险还不算大；撬墙要力气，旁边的瓦砾也可能跟着塌: Only a few hours pinned, so the risk of crush syndrome is still low; prying up the wall takes strength, and the rubble around it may come down too
strings.压得越久越危险，可搬开的那一刻也可能要他的命；撬房梁要力气，旁边的瓦砾随时会塌: The longer he’s pinned the worse it gets, but the moment the weight comes off could kill him; prying a beam takes strength, and the rubble around it could cave in any second
strings.压得越久，搬开那一刻越危险；再拖下去，冻也冻死了: The longer he’s pinned, the more dangerous the moment the weight comes off; wait any longer and the cold will kill him anyway
strings.压缩饼干被掰成小块，一个一个传了过去。: The hardtack is broken into little pieces and passed along, one by one.
strings.原型：2011 年 3 月 11 日东日本大地震。下午 14:46，宫城县外海发: Inspiration: the Great East Japan Earthquake of 11 March 2011. At 14:46 a magnitude 9.0 earthquake struck off Miyagi Prefecture, and thirty to forty minutes later the Sanriku coast was swallowed by a tsunami more than ten metres high, over 40 m in places. The Meteorological Agency’s first forecast was just “3 metres” and was raised only step by step; many people heard that first forecast and stayed at home or went upstairs. That night it snowed, temperatures fell below freezing, and soaked survivors died of hypothermia in large numbers; in Kesennuma and elsewhere the rubble and the oil tanks burned for days. Hilltop shrines and high ground saved many lives. At Okawa Elementary School, nearly 50 minutes lost arguing over where to flee cost 74 pupils their lives. In Kamaishi, schoolchildren who followed “tsunami tendenko” (when a tsunami comes, everyone runs for high ground on their own, without waiting for anyone) survived almost to a child, and when their first evacuation point looked unsafe they kept climbing higher. In Onagawa, the Japanese manager of a seafood company led 20 Chinese technical interns to high ground, then went back to look for his family and was killed. “Tsunami lung” from swallowed seawater and sludge; a radio as the only source of news once communications failed; and the long evacuations after the Fukushima nuclear accident, which killed far more elderly people—through moves, cold and stress—than the radiation itself: all of these are real too. The other inspiration is the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami: a sudden retreat of the sea is the sign that a tsunami is coming, and ten-year-old British girl Tilly Smith recognised it on a beach in Thailand, helping more than a hundred people get away in time. Shiomi is fictional.
strings.厦门一家医院的急诊科护士，干了十一年。来研修班是为了学大规模伤亡时的检伤分类。腰: An emergency-room nurse at a hospital in Xiamen for eleven years. She joined the course to learn triage for mass-casualty incidents. Her waist pack always holds a roll of tape and a pair of scissors.
strings.去搬，但先顾我们自己，别声张: Go, but look after ourselves first and keep it quiet
strings.去看看火和山上的老人: Go and check on the fire and the old people on the hill
strings.又一次余震。神社的木柱吱吱作响，雪从屋檐上簌簌地落下来。: Another aftershock. The shrine’s wooden pillars creak, and snow slides off the eaves.
strings.又一阵强余震。几分钟后，海边那个还能响的警报器拉响了海啸警报——下山的人还没有回: Another strong aftershock. A few minutes later, the one siren by the sea that still works sounds a tsunami warning—and the people who went down haven’t come back.
strings.又是一个睡不着的夜里。火堆边有人提议：每个人说一件这辈子最想再做一次的事。: Another sleepless night. By the fire, someone suggests that each of them name one thing they would most like to do again in this life.
strings.只给他后半段：从喊出“快跑”的那一秒开始: Give him only the second half, from the moment “Run!” is shouted
strings.各自往后山跑，别回头: Everyone run for the back of the hill—don’t look back
strings.名单念完了，没有姓小野寺的。葵说：“妈妈跑得很快的。”她没有哭。: The list comes to an end. No one named Onodera. Aoi says, “Mum runs really fast.” She doesn’t cry.
strings.后半夜，{actor} 头疼得厉害，吐了两回，叫也叫不醒——是一氧化碳中毒。有人: Later that night, {actor} has a splitting headache, throws up twice, and then can’t be woken—carbon monoxide poisoning. Someone rushes to throw open every door and window.
strings.后半夜，千代奶奶不说话了。她的手冰凉，嘴唇发紫，喊她只是哼一声。她身上那条毯子早: Late in the night, Granny Chiyo stops talking. Her hands are ice-cold, her lips blue, and when you call her name she only murmurs. The blanket over her has long since soaked through.
strings.后半夜，风向变了。港口那边的大火顺着瓦砾一路烧过来，山脚下的民宅一栋接一栋地着了: After midnight the wind shifts. The great fire by the harbour burns its way through the rubble; one house after another at the foot of the hill catches, and the wind carries sparks into the cedar woods on the slope. Watanabe watches the fire for a long time. “Once those cedars catch, it’ll be up here in half an hour.”
strings.后山有一条运木材的林道，翻过山梁往下走十八公里，就是内陆的町。地震以后路上全是塌: A logging road runs up behind the hill; over the ridge and eighteen kilometres down the other side is the inland town. Since the quake it is all landslides and fallen trees, and someone has to find out first which stretches are still passable.
strings.后来的人用得上；看过的人都会知道那一分钟: Those who come after can use it; everyone who watches will know about that minute
strings.后来，有人在八幡神社的石阶旁立了一块小木牌，上面写着 {actor} 的名字。木: Later, someone put up a small wooden marker beside the stone steps of the Hachiman Shrine with {actor}’s name on it. Next to it, someone no one knew had laid out an arrow of white pebbles pointing to the top of the hill.
strings.后面的浪来得没有声音。{actor} 没能跑回石阶。: The later wave comes without a sound. {actor} doesn’t make it back to the steps.
strings.听清楚再决定；可万一真的要跑，就晚了半天: Hear it out, then decide; but if you really do need to run, you’ll be half a day late
strings.听说在路上: Said to be on the way
strings.咬牙忍着，等救援队来: Grit your teeth and wait for the rescue team
strings.咱先把火整起来，有火就有主心骨。: Let’s get the fire going first. With a fire, people hold together.
strings.哪儿也不去：在雪地里长途跋涉，死的人会比辐射多: Go nowhere: a long trek through the snow would kill more people than radiation
strings.喝口热水吧，孩子。烫一点没关系。: Have some hot water, child. A little too hot won’t hurt you.
strings.喝完水等了一个钟头，房梁终于撬开了。阿部被抬上来的时候，一直在说女儿的名字。: They wait an hour after he drinks, and finally the beam comes up. All the way up the steps, Abe keeps saying his daughter’s name.
strings.喝：喝一口暖一暖: Drink: a mouthful to warm up
strings.嗓门不大但很稳，爱说“我们一件一件来”“先登记”。: A quiet but steady voice; likes “One thing at a time” and “Let’s register everyone first.”
strings.四个座位全给镇上的老人和孩子: All four seats to the town’s old people and children
strings.四个最虚弱的镇民被扶上了直升机。一个老太太在舱门口回头，冲屋檐下的你们双手合十。: The four frailest townspeople are helped into the helicopter. At the door an old woman turns back and presses her palms together toward you under the eaves.
strings.回去告诉大家，问问有没有人认识他: Go back, tell the others and ask if anyone knew him
strings.回来的路上碰上了强余震，{actor} 被倒下的墙压在了下面。: On the way back, a strong aftershock hits, and {actor} is buried under a falling wall.
strings.回来的路上，余震震塌了半截墙。{actor} 没能躲开。: On the way back, an aftershock brings down half a wall. {actor} can’t get clear.
strings.在 {actor} 的安排下，山上的镇民分成了几个组：有人捡柴，有人烧水，有人守: Under {actor}’s direction, the townspeople on the hill split into groups: some gather wood, some boil water, some watch over the old and the children.
strings.在塌方的林道上扭伤: sprained on a collapsed logging road
strings.在山上冻死、病死的镇民人数。: How many townspeople froze or died of illness on the hill.
strings.在潮见港打了六十年鱼。1960 年智利海啸那年他十七岁，眼看着海水退到港口外面又: Sixty years fishing out of Shiomi harbour. He was seventeen in the year of the 1960 Chile tsunami and watched the sea pull back past the harbour and come rushing in again. This afternoon he is the training centre’s guest speaker on “a fisherman’s experience of tsunamis,” with his shiba inu Kotaro along. His house is by the harbour, and his wife has bad legs.
strings.在瓦砾里一边喊一边听：被压住的人、困在半倒的房子里的人、泡在泥水里冻僵的人。找到: Shout and listen your way through the rubble: people pinned down, people trapped in half-collapsed houses, people frozen stiff in muddy water. Find one, and you still have to get them up the hill. On the first day the waves haven’t stopped, and at night you can’t see where you’re stepping.
strings.在神社下面的山坡上砍出一条十来米宽的隔离带：砍掉灌木和小树，把枯草、落叶扒到山下: Cut a strip ten-odd metres wide across the slope below the shrine: clear the brush and saplings, rake the dead grass and leaves to the downhill side. If the fire climbs up through the cedars, this is the only thing that can stop it.
strings.在神社前的空地上摆出 SOS 大字；摆好以后，要有人扫掉落在上面的雪、挂起神社的: Lay out a giant SOS on the open ground in front of the shrine. Once it’s done, someone has to keep sweeping the snow off it, hang up the shrine banners and make thick smoke with wet wood (one unit of firewood buys a while of smoke). Only if you can be seen will anyone come.
strings.在神社前的空地上，用床单、白色的泡沫板和瓦砾里的白漆板摆出几米高的 SOS。从直: Lay out an SOS several metres tall on the open ground in front of the shrine, using bedsheets, white foam boards and white-painted boards from the rubble. From a helicopter, it is the only thing that says “people here.”
strings.在篝火上架起仓库里的大锅，一锅一锅地化雪。一份木柴能化出三四升水，人要一直守在火: Set the big pot from the shed over the campfire and melt snow one potful after another. One unit of firewood gives three or four litres, and someone has to stay by the fire the whole time. Once the snow on the ground is gone, you will have to find another way.
strings.在背面写上：第二项，全员及格: Write on the back: Part two—everyone passes
strings.在青岛的消防救援站干了十八年，带过三茬新兵。来研修班学的是城市搜救。力气大，嗓门: Eighteen years at a fire-rescue station in Qingdao, three intakes of recruits trained. He joined the course to learn urban search and rescue. Strong and loud, with a phone always in his pocket; he wants to film everything to show his recruits back home.
strings.地震后是你第一个打开了收音机。广播里说“预计海啸高度三米”，你大声转述给了所有人: After the quake, you were the first to switch on the radio. The broadcast said “expected tsunami height: three metres,” and you repeated it loudly to everyone, adding, “The training centre has two floors. We’re fine.” A few minutes later you turned the radio off to save the batteries. Only later did you learn that in those few minutes the forecast had changed to “over ten metres.”
strings.地震摇起来的那一刻，你第一个冲出了研修中心的门。走廊里，当志愿者的高中生美咲被倒: The moment the shaking started, you were the first one out of the training centre’s door. In the corridor Misaki, the high school volunteer, tripped over a toppled cabinet and called out, and you didn’t look back. Someone else pulled her up. She doesn’t seem to have seen who it was.
strings.地震时你正在研修中心一楼的小卖部。往外跑之前，你把柜台上的两盒饼干、几块巧克力和: When the quake hit you were in the kiosk on the training centre’s ground floor. Before you ran, you stuffed two boxes of biscuits, a few chocolate bars and a bottle of water from the counter into your backpack, without paying and without telling anyone. They are still in your bag.
strings.坐到他身边，陪他把话说完: Sit down beside him and let him finish
strings.墙刚被撬开，{actor} 的脸一下子白了，抓着旁边人的手说了句“心口……”，就: The moment the wall comes up, {actor}’s face goes white. {actor.He} grabs the hand of the person beside {actor.him}—“My chest…”—and never lets go.
strings.外面的人不知道这里有人，就不会来；摆大字要很多人手: If no one outside knows we’re here, no one will come; laying out the letters takes a lot of hands
strings.外面的救援力量到达这里的进度。头一天几乎指望不上，之后越来越快；求救信号越醒目，: How close outside rescue is to reaching you. On the first day you can hardly count on it; after that it comes faster and faster, and the more visible your distress signal, the sooner you are found.
strings.外面的救援头一天几乎指望不上，之后一天比一天快。直升机只在白天、能见度好的时候来: Help from outside can hardly be counted on the first day, then comes faster each day. Helicopters fly only in daylight and good visibility, land only where they can see a distress signal on the ground, and take four people a trip; repairing the radio and making contact with the outside speeds rescue up a great deal. The Self-Defense Forces need three or four days to reach you. A long evacuation through the snow with old people can kill more on the road than staying would.
strings.多几双手，就能多找到几个人；可你们自己也快撑不住了: A few more pairs of hands means a few more people found; but you’re close to your own limit
strings.夜里会暖和很多；可这件事，{actor} 会记很久: Much warmer at night, but {actor} will remember this for a long time
strings.夜里涨潮了。沉下去的地面挡不住海水，低处的镇子又一次泡进了水里。山脚下一栋半淹的: The tide comes in during the night. The sunken ground can’t hold back the sea, and the low part of town floods again. In a half-submerged two-story building at the foot of the hill, someone is waving a flashlight.
strings.夜里，{actor} 听见 {name.p3} 那边有塑料包装纸窸窸窣窣的声音，: In the night, {actor} hears plastic wrapping rustle over where {name.p3} is lying, and a faint, sweet smell of chocolate drifts across.
strings.夜里，{actor} 坐在雪地上说想歇一会儿，就再也没有站起来。: In the night, {actor} sits down in the snow, says {actor.he} wants to rest a while, and never gets up again.
strings.夜里，又一波浪悄无声息地漫进了镇子，山脚下的瓦砾哗啦哗啦地响。: In the night another wave slides silently into the town; the rubble at the foot of the hill clatters and grinds.
strings.够全山的人吃好几天；可冷库挨着还在烧的油罐: Enough to feed the whole hill for days; but the cold store is right beside oil tanks that are still burning
strings.大嗓门，爱说“交给我”“别磨叽”，紧张时会骂一句粗话。: A big voice; likes “Leave it to me” and “Quit dawdling,” and swears once when he’s tense.
strings.大家一起挨饿，凭什么有人偷偷吃: Everyone is starving together; why should anyone eat in secret?
strings.大家从售货机旁边走了过去。: Everyone walks on past the vending machine.
strings.大家围着火坐着，谁也没有动。: Everyone sits around the fire. No one moves.
strings.大家守在石阶顶上，看着那盏手电一闪一闪。: Everyone waits at the top of the stone steps, watching the flashlight blink on and off.
strings.大家忽然发现葵不见了。有人看见她一个人顺着石阶往港口那边走，书包还背在身上——她: Suddenly everyone realizes Aoi is gone. Someone saw her heading down the stone steps toward the harbour alone, her school bag still on her back—she said she was going to wait for Mum outside the fish plant. The rubble below is still smoking.
strings.大家扶着 {protagonist} 一口一口喝完了水，又等了一个多钟头，才把撬: They hold {protagonist} up while {protagonist.he} drinks it all, sip by sip, then wait more than an hour before jamming the crowbars under the wall.
strings.大家把 {protagonist} 挪到火边，用毯子裹严实，轮流守着。: They move {protagonist} next to the fire, wrap {protagonist.him} tight in blankets and take turns keeping watch.
strings.大家把水一杯一杯地喂给 {protagonist}，喂到摇头，再接着喂。: Cup after cup, they feed {protagonist} water; when {protagonist.he} shakes {protagonist.his} head, they keep going.
strings.大家把水一杯一杯地喂给阿部，喂到他摇头，再接着喂。: Cup after cup, everyone feeds Abe water until he shakes his head, then keeps feeding him.
strings.大家把阿部挪到火边，用毯子把他裹严实，轮流守着。: Everyone moves Abe beside the fire, wraps him tight in blankets and takes turns watching him.
strings.大家用火柴棍抽了签。抽到长签的人愣了一下，才被拉上了直升机。: Everyone draws matchsticks. Those who get the long ones stand stunned for a moment before they are pulled into the helicopter.
strings.大家站在石阶顶上，看着那几股烟慢慢连成了一片。: Everyone stands at the top of the stone steps and watches the plumes of smoke slowly merge into one.
strings.大家缩回屋檐下，盯着山下的火光，谁也没再说话。: Everyone shrinks back under the eaves and watches the firelight below; no one says another word.
strings.大家都冷，顾不过来了: Everyone’s cold; you can’t look after everybody
strings.大家都这样，熬着吧: It’s the same for everyone; just tough it out
strings.大量补水能把毒素冲出去，是唯一能做的；可山上的水本来就不够: Plenty of fluids can flush the poisons out—it’s the only thing to do; but there was never enough water on the hill
strings.大量补水能把毒素冲出去；懂医的人在旁边守着更好: Plenty of fluid can flush out the toxins; better still with someone medical keeping watch
strings.天一亮，队伍就出发了。走在最前面的人，用树枝在雪地上一路划着记号。: At first light the column sets out. Whoever is in front scratches marks in the snow with a stick all along the way.
strings.天亮了看得清，水也退了；可那盏手电能亮到天亮吗: In daylight you can see and the water will be down, but will that flashlight last till dawn?
strings.天亮了，雪停了。从山顶望下去，潮见町没有了：从山脚一直到海边都是灰褐色的瓦砾，渔: Dawn comes, and the snow stops. From the top of the hill, Shiomi is gone: grey-brown rubble from the foot of the hill to the sea, fishing boats lying across what was the shopping street, black smoke still rising from the oil tanks at the harbour. On the radio, an announcer reads out casualty figures from town after town. Watanabe points behind the hill. “There’s a spring behind the shrine. The priest’s family used to get their water from it. The pipe’s probably broken.” In a corner of the shed, the town’s disaster radio lies where it fell, its antenna snapped.
strings.天亮时水退了，楼里的老人还活着，被扶上了山。: At dawn the water goes down. The old man in the building is still alive, and they help him up the hill.
strings.天亮时，那栋楼里没有手电光了。: By dawn, the flashlight in that building has gone dark.
strings.天亮的时候，有八个镇民背着包走进了后山的林子。后来听说，他们当中有两个老人没能走: At daybreak, eight townspeople shoulder their packs and walk into the woods behind the hill. Word comes later that two of the old people among them never made it inland.
strings.天压得很低，海风里一股油味和烂泥味。: The sky hangs low; the sea wind smells of oil and mud.
strings.天很蓝，冷得发脆。从山上望下去，一直到海边都是灰褐色的瓦砾。: A hard blue sky, brittle with cold. From the hill, grey-brown rubble runs all the way to the sea.
strings.天快亮的时候，两个人回来了，中间搀着一个浑身是泥的老太太——她在邻居家的二楼抱着: Toward dawn the two of them come back with an old woman between them, mud from head to foot—she spent the night on a neighbour’s second floor, clinging to a roof beam. Watanabe says nothing. He just holds her hand tight and doesn’t let go.
strings.天快亮的时候，阿部的呼吸停了。: Just before dawn, Abe stops breathing.
strings.天暖了一些，山顶上的雪化得差不多了。再想烧雪化水，就没有雪可铲了。: It has warmed up a little, and the snow on the hilltop has almost all melted. There is no more snow to shovel for water.
strings.天还没亮，几十个人排成一条长队，抬着担架钻进了后山的林道。: Before dawn, dozens of people set off in a long line up the logging road behind the hill, carrying stretchers.
strings.天黑以后，港口方向亮起了火光。泄漏的油罐、翻倒的汽车和压塌的房子烧了起来，火光映: After dark, firelight rises over the harbour. Leaking oil tanks, overturned cars and crushed houses are burning; the glow lights up the snow clouds until half the sky is red.
strings.天黑前，后山的石阶上爬上来一个背着红书包的小女孩，裤腿湿到了膝盖。她说她叫小野寺: Before dark, a little girl with a red school bag climbs the back steps of the hill, her trousers wet to the knees. She says her name is Onodera Aoi, third grade; her mother taught her that when a tsunami comes, she shouldn’t wait for Mum but run to the shrine on her own.
strings.天黑前，活下来的人一个一个爬上了八幡神社。: Before dark, the survivors climb up to the Hachiman Shrine one by one.
strings.天黑透了，雪越下越大。社务所和防灾仓库里挤了 {var.crowd}，连坐的地方: It’s completely dark now, and the snow is getting heavier. The shrine office and the supply shed are packed with {var.crowd}, with no room even to sit, and you outsiders are left under the drafty eaves. The shed holds only thirty-odd blankets and a box of relief tracksuits. The soaked ones are shaking in the snow, their lips already blue.
strings.太危险了：油罐随时会炸: Too dangerous: the oil tanks could blow any minute
strings.头脑清楚、嘴硬心软，最讨厌被人当成累赘。疼也不说，冷也不说，只会问别人冷不冷。: Clear-headed, sharp-tongued and soft-hearted, and she hates being treated as a burden. She never says when she’s in pain or cold; she only asks whether everyone else is cold.
strings.她才九岁；可瞒着她，她迟早会知道: She’s only nine; but keep it from her and she’ll find out sooner or later
strings.她有权知道；所有人也都会知道: She has a right to know, and everyone else will know too
strings.她的姐妹们会先走；山上离不开一个会两种话的人: Her friends from the plant leave first; the hill can’t do without someone who speaks both languages
strings.她能暖过来；脱外套的人今晚要挨冻: She’ll warm up; whoever gives up the coat freezes tonight
strings.她走；三个空座让给最虚弱的老人和伤员: She leaves; the three spare seats go to the frailest old people and the injured
strings.她走；空座给我们自己人: She leaves; the spare seats go to our own people
strings.妈妈在水产厂上班。她跑得很快的。: Mum works at the fish plant. She runs really fast.
strings.妈妈说，海啸来了不要等她。我没等。: Mum said, when a tsunami comes, don’t wait for her. I didn’t wait.
strings.孙丽娜一直站在石阶口往下望。她说，地震时是厂长佐佐木带着她们十九个人跑上山的。把: Lina Sun has been standing at the head of the stone steps all this time, looking down. She says it was the plant manager, Sasaki, who led the other nineteen interns up the hill when the quake struck. Once he had got them to the shrine, he turned and ran back down—his wife and his daughter, still in elementary school, were at home. “He said, ‘You go on up. Don’t wait for me.’”
strings.孙丽娜一笔一画地写下了佐佐木一家三口的名字，又用日语写了一遍。: Stroke by careful stroke, Lina Sun writes out the names of all three Sasakis, then writes them again in Japanese.
strings.孙丽娜上了领事馆的大巴。: Lina Sun boards the consulate bus.
strings.孙丽娜上了领事馆的大巴。车开动的时候，她把脸贴在车窗上，朝山上挥了很久的手。: Lina Sun boards the consulate bus. As it pulls away, she presses her face to the window and waves up at the hill for a long time.
strings.孙丽娜上了领事馆的大巴，一路扶着担架。: Lina Sun boards the consulate bus and keeps a hand on a stretcher the whole way.
strings.孙丽娜低下头，往角落里缩了缩。: Lina Sun lowers her head and shrinks farther into the corner.
strings.孙丽娜又看了冷库一眼，点点头：“也是。”: Lina Sun takes one more look at the cold store and nods. “Fair enough.”
strings.孙丽娜和厂里的十九个姐妹是坐领事馆的大巴走的，在新潟坐上了回大连的飞机。到家那天: Lina Sun and the nineteen others from the plant left on the consulate’s bus and flew home to Dalian from Niigata. On the day she got home, her mother waited all afternoon downstairs. The next year she used her savings to open a small restaurant in Donggang. On the wall hangs a group photo: twenty young women on the stone steps of the Hachiman Shrine, smiling with an effort.
strings.孙丽娜在潮见又留了三个月，给自卫队和志愿者当翻译。厂长佐佐木的遗体是四月找到的。: Lina Sun stayed in Shiomi another three months, interpreting for the Self-Defense Forces and the volunteers. The body of Sasaki, the plant manager, was found in April. At the funeral twenty Chinese women stood in a row and bowed, and Lina Sun read a eulogy in Japanese; when she got to “You go on up, don’t wait for me,” she stopped for a long time.
strings.孙丽娜把姐妹们一个一个送上车，自己留了下来。大巴开走以后，她在石阶上坐了很久。: Lina Sun sees her friends onto the bus one by one and stays behind herself. After it pulls away, she sits on the stone steps for a long time.
strings.孙丽娜把姐妹们叫到一起，用日语和中文各说了一遍。: Lina Sun gathers the other women from the plant and says it twice, once in Japanese and once in Chinese.
strings.孙丽娜望着港口边水产厂那栋只剩骨架的冷库：“里面有好几千罐秋刀鱼和鲭鱼罐头，冻鱼: Lina Sun gazes at the fish plant’s cold store down by the harbour, a bare skeleton now. “There are thousands of cans of saury and mackerel in there, tons of frozen fish too. Cans are still good after a soaking.” She pauses. “If the boss was here, he’d tell everyone to help themselves. But he’s gone.” The cold store is little more than a hundred metres from the oil tanks, which are still smoking.
strings.孙丽娜的骨灰被送回了辽宁东港。厂里的十九个姐妹在她的遗像前放了一罐秋刀鱼罐头，罐: Lina Sun’s ashes were sent home to Donggang, Liaoning. The nineteen women from the plant set a can of saury in front of her photograph, with a handwritten label on it: Shiomi.
strings.孩子，我这把老骨头，不值得你们拼命。: Child, these old bones aren’t worth risking your lives for.
strings.守在神社这边，盯着火，别让它烧上来: Stay up at the shrine and keep an eye on the fire; don’t let it climb
strings.安静、懂事得让人心疼，总说“我没事”。夜里会突然醒过来，问妈妈是不是也在往山上跑: Quiet and heartbreakingly well-behaved, always saying “I’m fine.” At night she wakes with a start and asks whether her mum is running up a hill too.
strings.安静、沉得住气，习惯先看地形再说话；对人对事都很直，不会撒谎，一撒谎就脸红。: Quiet and steady; she reads the terrain before she speaks. Straight with people and things—she can’t lie, and blushes when she tries.
strings.实习生们一个一个上了车。孙丽娜最后一个上去，在车门口回头鞠了一躬。: The interns board one by one. Lina Sun is the last on; at the door she turns and bows.
strings.实习生们扶着养老院的老人，跟着你们往神社跑。水产厂的厂长佐佐木把人送到石阶底下，: The interns help the nursing-home residents along and follow you toward the shrine. Sasaki, the plant manager, sees everyone to the bottom of the steps, then turns and runs back toward the harbour—his house is down there.
strings.家里人不知道你还活着: Your family doesn’t know you’re alive
strings.对她说：渡边老人讲过，海啸来了各自跑，活下来的人不许怪自己: Tell her what Watanabe said: when a tsunami comes, everyone runs on their own, and whoever lives is not allowed to blame themselves
strings.小卖部的事，{actor} 谁也没告诉。半年后，潮见町在临时板房里开了一条商店街: {actor} never told anyone about the kiosk. Six months later Shiomi opened a shopping street in temporary prefab buildings. {actor} sent an envelope with far more money than two boxes of biscuits, unsigned. The woman who ran the kiosk taped the envelope to the wall behind her till.
strings.小声说话，句子很短：“妈妈说，不要等她。”“我没哭。”: Speaks softly, in very short sentences: “Mum said not to wait for her.” “I’m not crying.”
strings.小太郎后来被内陆的一户人家收养了。它很快就习惯了新家，只是每次听见警报声，都会钻: Kotaro was later taken in by a family inland. He settled into his new home quickly, except that whenever he heard a siren he crawled under the table, laid his chin on his front paws and waited without moving.
strings.小太郎在前面跑，渡边老人在后面喊。不到半个钟头，狗把葵领了回来——它一路咬着她的: Kotaro runs ahead with Watanabe shouting after him. In less than half an hour the dog leads Aoi back—holding the hem of her coat in his teeth all the way.
strings.小太郎在瓦砾里转了几圈，自己跑了回来。过了好几个钟头，下山的人才在港口边找到冻僵: Kotaro circles through the rubble a few times and comes back on his own. Hours later, the people who went down find Aoi by the harbour, half-frozen.
strings.小太郎没能走下那座山。有人在神社后面的杉树下给它垒了一个小小的石堆，上面压着一根: Kotaro never made it down from the hill. Someone built him a little cairn under the cedars behind the shrine and laid on top of it the bamboo stick he loved to carry.
strings.小太郎突然冲着山脚下一堆瓦砾狂叫，叫一阵，跑回来扯渡边老人的裤腿，再跑回去接着叫: Kotaro suddenly starts barking furiously at a pile of rubble at the foot of the hill. He barks for a while, runs back to tug at Watanabe’s trouser leg, then runs back and barks some more.
strings.小太郎跟着回来了，浑身是泥，一瘸一拐。: Kotaro comes back with him, muddy all over and limping.
strings.小太郎跟着渡边老人住进了临时板房。每天早上，一老一狗爬一趟八幡神社的石阶。它再也: Kotaro moved into the temporary prefab with Watanabe. Every morning the old man and the dog climbed the steps of the Hachiman Shrine together. He never chased seagulls again, but every time he reached the top he barked once at the sea, as if checking on something.
strings.小太郎，过来。别往下跑。: Kotaro, here. Don’t go down there.
strings.就在仓库里点上：先暖和过来再说: Light it right here in the shed: get warm first, worry later
strings.山上一个像是町议员的老人挨个问大家：“有没有人拍到海啸来之前的样子？防灾研究所以: An old man on the hill who looks like a town councillor goes from person to person asking, “Did anyone film what it looked like before the tsunami came? The Disaster Prevention Institute will need it.” The video is still on {actor}’s phone: the sea drawn back past the harbour, {actor.his} own voice saying “Look at that,” and almost a minute before the shout of “Run!”
strings.山上冻死、饿死的人会少；可你们自己的那份会少得很快: Fewer people on the hill will freeze or starve, but your own share will shrink fast
strings.山上几十张嘴，分下去每人一口；不声张，你们几个能吃饱: Dozens of mouths on the hill—shared out, it’s a mouthful each; keep it quiet and the few of you eat your fill
strings.山上又有 {var.tmp} 个镇民没能熬过去，大多是老人。有人把他们抬到神社后: {var.tmp} more of the townspeople on the hill have not made it, most of them old. Someone carries them to the cedars behind the shrine and covers them with blankets.
strings.山上又有一个镇民没能熬过去，是个老人。有人把遗体抬到神社后面的杉树下，盖上了毯子: One more of the townspeople on the hill has not made it—an old one. Someone carries the body to the cedars behind the shrine and covers it with a blanket.
strings.山上已经有人咳出黑色的痰，发着高烧，喘气时胸口呼噜作响——在浪里呛进去的淤泥进了: Some on the hill are already coughing up black phlegm, burning with fever, their chests rattling as they breathe—the sludge they swallowed in the wave has reached their lungs. Without antibiotics, pneumonia like this can kill within days. The nearest medicine is in the ruins of the clinic, two kilometres away.
strings.山上死去的镇民: Townspeople who died on the hill
strings.山上的人都站在石阶顶上，往海的方向看。: Everyone on the hill stands at the top of the stone steps, looking toward the sea.
strings.山上的水和吃的撑不过今天；可那些东西都是别人家的: The water and food on the hill won’t last the day; but all of that belongs to someone
strings.山上的镇民后来说，那个一直在登记名字的外国人，最后一页还没写完。那个小本子交给了: The townspeople said later that the foreigner who kept registering names never finished the last page. The little notebook went to the town hall and is now in Shiomi’s earthquake archive.
strings.山上的镇民，不能有太多人冻死、病死在你眼前（死去的不超过 3 人）: Don’t let too many of the townspeople on the hill freeze or die of sickness in front of you (no more than 3)
strings.山下还有人在瓦砾里找亲人: There are still people below, searching the rubble for their families
strings.山地救援队的向导: Guide with a mountain rescue team
strings.山脚下“轰”的一声巨响，一个煤气罐炸上了天，带着火的碎木头像雨点一样落在山坡上。: A huge boom at the foot of the hill: a gas cylinder blows sky-high, and burning splinters rain down on the slope. Plumes of smoke rise at the edge of the cedar woods.
strings.山脚下那栋民宿的瓦砾里，再也没有敲击声了。: From the rubble of the guesthouse at the foot of the hill, there is no more knocking.
strings.山脚下，一栋被海啸推出两百多米的民宿歪在一辆翻倒的卡车上。瓦砾深处传来有气无力的: At the foot of the hill, a guesthouse the tsunami shoved more than two hundred metres sits askew on an overturned truck. From deep in the rubble comes a feeble knocking. Pull away a few boards and a hand appears in the gap—a man’s legs are pinned under a beam, half his body in freezing muddy water. He says his name is Abe, and he has been pinned since the afternoon, nearly {hours} hours.
strings.山脚下，半倒的房子在余震里又塌了一截，{actor} 被压在碎木头底下，是旁边的: At the foot of the hill, a half-collapsed house sags further in the aftershock and {actor} is pinned under broken timber until the people nearby dig {actor.him} out.
strings.山脚下，半倒的房子在余震里整个塌了下来。{actor} 没能跑出来。: At the foot of the hill, a half-collapsed house comes down completely in the aftershock. {actor} doesn’t get out.
strings.山脚下，阿部已经被压了 {var.abe_h}。去看过他的人说，他还在跟人开玩笑: At the foot of the hill, Abe has been pinned for {var.abe_h} now. Those who have been down to see him say he is still cracking jokes, but his lips are purple and his hands won’t stop shaking. “Pry it up… I can take it.”
strings.带人下去扑灭山坡上的火点: Take people down to put out the spot fires on the slope
strings.带所有人往后山更高的地方转移，等警报解除: Lead everyone higher up behind the hill until the warning is lifted
strings.干干净净；可山上的水不够: Clean hands, but there isn’t enough water on the hill
strings.年轻力壮的先走，老人和伤员留下等救援: The young and fit go first; the old and injured stay and wait for rescue
strings.年轻母亲接过饼干，鞠了一躬，先掰了一小块塞进孩子嘴里。: The young mother takes the hardtack with a bow and, before anything else, breaks off a small piece and tucks it into her child’s mouth.
strings.年轻母亲点点头，抱着孩子走回了人群里。: The young mother nods and carries her child back into the crowd.
strings.广播说浪高三米，研修中心有两层：先上二楼，等下一次广播: The broadcast says three metres and the training centre has two floors: go upstairs and wait for the next announcement
strings.广播里说得很清楚：撤离范围是核电站周围二十公里，这里离那里一百二十多公里，这几天: The broadcast is clear: the evacuation zone is twenty kilometres around the plant, this hill is more than a hundred and twenty kilometres away, and the wind has been from the north for days. Little by little, the talk around the fire dies down. Only three people shoulder their packs and leave anyway.
strings.床单、白色的泡沫板、仓库的白铁皮……能用的白东西全被拖到了神社前的空地上。: Bedsheets, white foam boards, sheets of white metal from the shed… anything white is dragged onto the open ground in front of the shrine.
strings.强余震！地面又一次横着甩起来，神社前的石灯笼倒了一排，社务所的瓦片哗哗地往下掉。: A strong aftershock! The ground whips sideways again; a row of stone lanterns in front of the shrine topples, and tiles slide off the shrine office roof.
strings.当场揭穿: Call it out on the spot
strings.当着大家的面，说出那句话是自己说的: Admit in front of everyone that those words were yours
strings.快；可老板就在旁边看着: Quick, but the owner is right there watching
strings.急救课上讲过：湿衣服比雪还要命。只是要在一屋子人面前脱光，换上不合身的单衣: The first-aid course said it: wet clothes kill faster than snow. Only it means stripping in front of a room full of people and pulling on thin clothes that don’t fit
strings.慢上几分钟。投这个选项的人去抬轮椅、去喊人，会是最后一批上山的，可能被浪追上: A few minutes slower. Whoever votes for this carries the wheelchair and goes knocking, and will be the last up the hill—the wave may catch them
strings.慢悠悠的，爱叫年轻人“孩子”：“孩子，我这把老骨头，不值得你们拼命。”: Unhurried; calls young people “child”: “Child, these old bones aren’t worth risking your lives for.”
strings.慢，可没有人会被丢下: Slow, but no one gets left behind
strings.成都一家通信公司的基站工程师，业余无线电爱好者，呼号背得比身份证号还熟。来研修班: A base-station engineer at a telecom company in Chengdu and a ham radio enthusiast who knows his call sign better than his ID number. He joined the course to learn emergency communications. Thin, glasses, a backpack stuffed with a power bank, a multimeter and a roll of electrical tape.
strings.我以后要当护士。今天这些，就当实习了。: I’m going to be a nurse. Today can count as practice.
strings.我们也是人：挤进社务所里去，毯子按人头分: We’re people too: squeeze into the shrine office and share the blankets out by head
strings.我们先走：我们是外地人，留下来只会多占一份口粮: We go first: we’re outsiders, and staying just means one more mouth to feed
strings.我们受过训练：跟着他们一起下山搜救: We’re trained for this: go down with them and search
strings.我们最后走：等山上的镇民都上了车: We go last: once every townsperson on the hill is aboard
strings.我修了二十年屋顶，头一回躺在屋顶底下。: Twenty years fixing roofs, and this is my first time lying under one.
strings.我去！老人那边交给我。: I’ll go! Leave the old folks to me.
strings.我女儿在仙台念大学，学建筑的，说以后要盖冲不走的房子。: My daughter’s at university in Sendai, studying architecture. Says she’ll build houses the sea can’t take.
strings.我妈要是看见新闻，得急疯了。手机还是没信号？: If my mum sees the news she’ll go out of her mind. Still no signal on the phones?
strings.我妈说，山那边的人会来接我们的。: Mum says people will come over the mountain to get us.
strings.我家老太婆……腿不好。……不说了。: My old woman… her legs are bad. …Never mind.
strings.我弟明年高考。我这一年半挣的钱，够他念完大学了。: My brother sits his college entrance exam next year. What I’ve earned in a year and a half is enough to get him through university.
strings.我接生过的孩子，今天不知道还剩几个。: All the babies I delivered—I wonder how many are left today.
strings.房梁“咔”地往下一沉，{actor} 的手被夹在了下面。阿部疼得骂了一句，又笑：: The beam drops with a crack, and {actor}’s hand is caught under it. Abe swears with the pain, then laughs. “Take it easy. I can still hold on.”
strings.房梁刚撬开，阿部的脸一下子白了，抓着 {actor} 的手说了句“心口……”，就: The instant the beam comes up, Abe goes white, grips {actor}’s hand and says, “My chest…,” and never lets go.
strings.房梁撬开了。阿部被抬上石阶的时候，冲大家竖了一下大拇指。: The beam comes up. As Abe is carried up the steps, he gives everyone a thumbs-up.
strings.房梁撬开的那一刻，阿部抓住 {actor} 的袖子，嘴张了张，什么也没说出来。: The instant the beam comes up, Abe grabs {actor}’s sleeve; his mouth opens, but nothing comes out.
strings.房梁撬开的那一刻，阿部抽搐了一下，就没了声音。旁边的人按了很久他的胸口。: The moment the beam comes up, Abe jerks once and falls silent. The people beside him press on his chest for a long time.
strings.所有人一起走：老人和伤员用担架抬: Everyone goes together, carrying the old and the injured on stretchers
strings.所有人上，连夜把防火带开完: All hands: finish the firebreak overnight
strings.所有人分头去找，一边走一边喊她的名字: Everyone split up and search, calling her name
strings.所有人用桶装雪，浇湿屋顶和屋檐: Everyone fill buckets with snow and soak the roofs and eaves
strings.所有人都在往后山的林子里跑，没有人回头。: Everyone is running into the woods behind the hill. No one looks back.
strings.所有能动的人冒雪下山捡木头，今晚无论如何要把篝火烧起来: Everyone who can move goes down through the snow for wood—tonight, whatever it takes, we get a fire going
strings.手机在镇民手里一个一个地传。有个老人打通了儿子的电话，什么也没说，只是一直点头。: The phone passes from one townsperson to the next. One old man gets through to his son and says nothing at all, just keeps nodding.
strings.手水舍的竹管里先是滴了几滴，接着“哗”地一下流了出来。水很凉，有一点土腥味。几个: A few drops fall from the bamboo spout of the fountain, then it gushes. The water is cold, with a faint taste of earth. Some of the old people cup it in their hands to drink, and start crying as they drink.
strings.手电光照过去，{name.p3} 的手里攥着半块巧克力，背包敞着口。: The flashlight beam swings over: {name.p3} is clutching half a chocolate bar, backpack gaping open.
strings.手电的光在雪里只照得见两步远。你们一趟一趟地把湿木头拖上石阶，劈开，塞进火里。: The flashlight beams reach two steps into the snow. Trip after trip, you drag wet wood up the steps, split it and feed it to the fire.
strings.托灾害对策本部和自卫队帮忙查她妈妈的下落: Ask the town disaster headquarters and the Self-Defense Forces to trace her mother
strings.找了很久才找到葵。她蹲在一辆翻倒的车后面，冻得说不出话。: It takes a long time to find Aoi. She is crouched behind an overturned car, too cold to speak.
strings.找到葵的时候，她的腿被碎玻璃划了一道大口子，一声也没哭。: When they find Aoi, broken glass has cut a long gash in her leg. She hasn’t cried once.
strings.把东西还给他，道个歉: Give it back to him and apologize
strings.把厂长一家的名字写进寻人名单，托外面的人打听: Add the manager’s family to the missing-persons list and ask outside for news
strings.把她挪到篝火边，烧一壶热水给她暖着（用掉 1 份木柴）: Move her to the campfire and boil some water to warm her (uses 1 unit of firewood)
strings.把它叫回来：下面还在冒烟，太危险: Call him back: it’s still smoking down there, too dangerous
strings.把手机传给山上的镇民，让他们给家里报平安: Pass the phone around so the townspeople can tell their families they’re safe
strings.把手机里那段视频活着带出去，交给研究海啸的人: Get the video on your phone out alive and hand it to people who study tsunamis
strings.把收音机放到中间，陪她一起听到最后（用掉 1 节电池）: Put the radio in the middle and listen to the end with her (uses 1 AA battery)
strings.把棉袄脱下来：活人比死人更需要它: Take the padded coat: the living need it more than the dead
strings.把水给 {protagonist} 灌下去，能喝多少喝多少（用掉 3 升水）: Pour water into {protagonist}, as much as {protagonist.he} can drink (uses 3 L of water)
strings.把水给他灌下去，能喝多少喝多少（用掉 3 升水）: Pour water into him, as much as he can drink (uses 3 L of water)
strings.把火边最暖的位置和热水都给病人（用掉 3 升水）: Give the sick the warmest places by the fire and all the hot water (uses 3 L of water)
strings.把病人挪到仓库另一头，挖一个新的厕所坑，喝的水一律烧开（用掉 1 份木柴）: Move the sick to the far end of the shed, dig a new latrine pit and boil all drinking water (uses 1 unit of firewood)
strings.抓紧时间睡一会儿: Grab some sleep while you can
strings.投这个选项的人先上飞机（最多四个）；留下的人会记住这一刻: Whoever votes for this boards first (four at most); those left behind will remember this moment
strings.投这个选项的人翻山先走；留下的人要靠自己熬到救援来: Whoever votes for this crosses the mountain first; those who stay must hold out on their own until rescue comes
strings.抽屉里的一盒电池: A box of batteries in a drawer
strings.担架一副一副地抬下了石阶。: Stretcher after stretcher goes down the stone steps.
strings.拆下了社务所旁边的一段木栅栏: Pulled down a stretch of wooden fence beside the shrine office
strings.拆社务所旁边的木栅栏、旧木板和参道两旁的长凳当柴烧。不用下山，干木头一点就着；可: Pull down the wooden fence beside the shrine office, the old boards and the benches along the shrine approach for firewood. No trip down the hill, and dry wood catches at once—but there is only so much of it, and some of the townspeople won’t like it.
strings.拦住他：“てんでんこ”是您教我们的——她一定也自己跑了: Stop him: “tendenko”—you taught us that yourself; she will have run on her own too
strings.拿到避风棚里点，留着通风口: Light it in the windbreak shelter and leave a vent open
strings.拿着仓库里的锹和锯，在山腰上砍出一条隔离带：砍灌木、锯小树、扒开枯草。火在山下烧: Take the shovels and saws from the shed and cut a firebreak across the hillside: chop the brush, saw the saplings, rake away the dead grass. The fire is burning below, and whoever does this work is closest to it.
strings.指示灯亮了。喇叭里沙沙响了一阵，传出一个人声：“这里是町灾害对策本部，八幡神社请: The indicator light comes on. The speaker hisses for a while, then a human voice: “This is the town disaster headquarters. Hachiman Shrine, please respond!” Someone puts a hand over their mouth.
strings.按组撤到后山：先背老人和孩子，最后一个人点名: Fall back behind the hill in groups: carry the old and the children first, someone at the rear counting heads
strings.按规定去指定避难所：三百米外的潮见小学，三层楼: Follow the rules and go to the designated shelter: Shiomi Elementary, three stories, three hundred metres away
strings.挑“身体最差的人”时用。: Used to pick “whoever is in the worst shape.”
strings.探出来的那条林道还在：翻过山梁往下走十八公里，就是内陆的町，听说那里有自卫队的营: The logging road the scouts found is still open: over the ridge and eighteen kilometres down is the inland town, where the Self-Defense Forces are said to have a camp. The way is all snow and fallen trees, a full day’s walk. And there are still old people and injured on the hill who can’t walk.
strings.探翻山的路: Scout the road over the mountain
strings.探路的人回来了，裤腿上全是泥和雪：林道塌了两处，可绕得过去。翻过山梁往下走十八公: The scouts come back with mud and snow up to their knees: the logging road has collapsed in two places, but you can get around. Over the ridge and eighteen kilometres down is the inland town, where the Self-Defense Forces are said to have a camp.
strings.摆 SOS、打信号: Lay out the SOS and signal
strings.摇晃来之前的几秒钟，小太郎突然站起来低吼——几个人下意识地护住了头。: Seconds before the shaking, Kotaro suddenly stands and growls—several people cover their heads without thinking.
strings.撕下来引火：纸是干的: Tear them off for kindling: the paper’s dry enough
strings.撬开的自动售货机里的几瓶茶和矿泉水: A few bottles of tea and water from a pried-open vending machine
strings.撬棍一插，铁门就开了。老板把烟头扔在地上，转身走了。: One jab of the crowbar and the metal door springs open. The owner throws down his cigarette butt, turns and walks away.
strings.撬棍滑了，房梁又沉回去一截。阿部疼得昏了过去。: The crowbar slips and the beam sinks back down a notch. Abe passes out from the pain.
strings.收好它，带回去: Keep it safe and take it home
strings.收音机和手电用的五号电池。收音机是唯一能听到外面消息的东西。: AA batteries for the radio and the flashlight. The radio is the only way to hear news from outside.
strings.收音机的事说出来以后，有人很久没有跟 {actor} 说话。后来，{actor}: After the radio came out, some people didn’t speak to {actor} for a long time. Later, back in {actor.his} own neighbourhood, {actor} pushed through one small change: a slip of paper taped to every emergency radio—“Forecasts change. Don’t stop at the first one.”
strings.收音机被关掉了。葵看了看收音机，又看了看大家，什么也没问。: The radio is switched off. Aoi looks at the radio, then at everyone, and asks nothing.
strings.收音机里开始念各个避难所报上来的名单：名字、年龄、在哪个避难所。念到“潮见町，内: The radio starts reading out the lists the shelters have sent in: name, age, which shelter. When it reaches “Shiomi, inland junior high school gym,” everyone holds their breath. Aoi grips the straps of her school bag and doesn’t move.
strings.收音机里断断续续地说：南边的核电站发生了爆炸，政府要求周围二十公里内的居民撤离。: Through the static, the radio says there has been an explosion at the nuclear plant to the south, and the government has ordered everyone within twenty kilometres to evacuate. Around the fire, panic boils over at once: some say the radiation will blow in on the sea wind, and everyone must cross the mountains inland right now. But the plant is more than a hundred kilometres away, the logging road over the ridge is still buried in snow, and there are people in their eighties on the hill, and injured who can’t walk.
strings.放一把逆火：先把防火带下面的草烧掉，让两股火撞在一起: Set a backfire: burn off the grass below the firebreak and let the two fires meet
strings.救得了眼前这一个: You can save the one in front of you
strings.救援队有输液和液压顶杆: The rescue team has IV drips and hydraulic jacks
strings.敲响神社的钟，打手电，让他们知道: Ring the shrine bell and flash lights so they know
strings.敲响神社的钟，给山下的人报信: Ring the shrine bell to warn the people below
strings.日本老太太跟我说谢谢，我都不知道怎么回。: The old Japanese ladies keep thanking me, and I never know what to say back.
strings.暖和得少一些，可不会憋死人: Less warmth, but no one suffocates
strings.暖炉放在了避风棚的中间，防水布的一角掀开了一条缝。: The heater goes in the middle of the windbreak shelter, with one corner of the tarp lifted to leave a gap.
strings.暖炉的火苗蓝幽幽的，仓库里一下子暖和了。: The heater’s flame burns a soft, eerie blue, and the shed warms up at once.
strings.最危险的人先走；能抬担架的队员就那么几个: Those in the most danger go first; there are only so many troops to carry stretchers
strings.最后一个人离开八幡神社的时候，回头看了一眼雪地上的 SOS。{survivors: The last one to leave the Hachiman Shrine looked back once at the SOS in the snow. {survivors}—almost every one of them. In Shiomi’s disaster report for that year, the page on the Hachiman Shrine was short. Three months later, the course mailed the belated certificates to everyone’s homes, dated that Friday. None of you ever hung yours up, but every March, at about the same time, you sent each other a message.
strings.最后一辆卡车开走的时候，八幡神社的山顶上只剩下一堆熄灭的篝火，和雪地上的 SOS: When the last truck pulls away, all that is left on the Hachiman Shrine hilltop is a burnt-out campfire and the SOS in the snow.
strings.最后几级台阶，浪追上了 {actor}。水退下去以后，石阶上只剩一只鞋。: On the last few steps, the wave catches {actor}. When the water drains away, there is only a shoe on the steps.
strings.最快，你们几个肯定来得及。可轮椅上的千代奶奶、隔壁水产厂和养老院的人，只能靠他们: The fastest; the five of you will certainly make it. But Granny Chiyo in her wheelchair and the people in the fish plant and the nursing home are on their own
strings.最稳妥，也最符合救援规范；可他得泡在冰冷的泥水里，一直熬到救援队来: The safest course and the one the rescue rules call for; but he will have to lie in the freezing mud until the rescuers arrive
strings.最符合救援规范；可要在冰冷的瓦砾里一直被压着: By the book, but it means staying pinned in the freezing rubble
strings.最虚弱的十几个老人先被抬下了山。剩下的人裹上了自卫队带来的毯子。: The dozen or so frailest old people are carried down the hill first. The rest are wrapped in the blankets the SDF brought.
strings.最要紧的是人；可今天下山的人，就干不了别的了: People come first; but whoever goes down today can’t do anything else
strings.最需要医院的人先去医院；剩下的座位给镇上病得最重的老人: Those who most need a hospital get there first; any seats left go to the sickest old people from town
strings.有了火，湿衣服才烤得干；可雪夜里下山看不清脚下，海啸警报也还没解除: With a fire, wet clothes can dry; but on a snowy night you can’t see your feet, and the tsunami warning hasn’t been lifted
strings.有人一直数着 {protagonist} 的脉搏，一杯一杯地喂水。天亮时，尿的颜: Someone keeps counting {protagonist}’s pulse as the water goes in, cup after cup. By daybreak the urine has turned paler.
strings.有人背起老人，有人抱起孩子，一组一组地往后山撤。: Some carry the old on their backs, some carry children in their arms, and group by group they fall back behind the hill.
strings.有时候，有人陪着就够了: Sometimes it’s enough just to have someone there
strings.有用的部分都在；那一分钟，只有自己知道: Everything useful is there; that minute stays yours alone
strings.机灵、认生，只听渡边的。余震来之前的几秒钟，它总会竖起耳朵低吼。鼻子很灵。: Clever and wary of strangers; he listens to no one but Watanabe. In the seconds before an aftershock he always pricks up his ears and growls. A very good nose.
strings.机组人员先扔下来两箱矿泉水和一箱压缩饼干。: The crew first throw down two cases of bottled water and a case of hardtack.
strings.机组人员抬着担架，弯着腰钻进了雪雾。: Bent low, the crew carry the stretchers into the whirling snow.
strings.机组人员看了你们一眼，什么也没说，伸手把人拉了上去。: The crew give you one look, say nothing, and reach out to pull people aboard.
strings.杭州一个街道应急管理办公室的副主任，组织过台风撤离，管过临时安置点，跟老人打交道: Deputy head of a neighbourhood emergency management office in Hangzhou; she has organized typhoon evacuations and run temporary shelters, and old people are her strong suit. She joined the course to learn shelter management. She carries a little notebook full of phone numbers.
strings.林道上的雪又积厚了一层。: Another layer of snow settles on the logging road.
strings.柜子全被冲空了，只剩一地泡烂的文件: Cabinets swept empty, nothing but a floor of soggy paperwork
strings.棉袄还是湿的，带着泥腥味。{actor} 拧了半天，穿在了身上。: The coat is still wet and smells of mud. {actor} wrings it out for a long time, then puts it on.
strings.止血带勒上了，房梁却怎么也撬不动，{actor} 的手还被夹了一下。: The tourniquets are on, but the beam won’t budge, and {actor}’s hand gets caught for good measure.
strings.止血带能拦住压坏的肌肉里的毒素，多半能保住命；可勒上几个小时，腿多半保不住: A tourniquet holds back the poisons from the crushed muscle and will probably save his life; but a few hours of it and he will probably lose the legs
strings.此前的八场推演里，你们在雪山、怒海、矿井、废墟、沙漠、孤岛、极夜和洪水里一次次“: In the eight simulations before this one, you “died” again and again—on a snowy mountain, on a raging sea, in a flooded mine, in rubble, in the desert, on an island, in the polar night and in a flood—and sat back up each time the examiner called “end of simulation.” The training centre is a two-story building less than a hundred metres from the sea. Behind it rises a small hill, and on top are the Hachiman Shrine and the town’s emergency supply shed, thirty metres above sea level, circled in red on the hazard map as the tsunami evacuation site. The town’s other designated shelter is Shiomi Elementary School, three hundred metres from the sea: three stories, the roof about twelve metres up.
strings.毯子一条一条传了出去。千代奶奶把自己那条往美咲身上推，被按了回去。屋檐下，你们几: The blankets are passed out one by one. Granny Chiyo pushes hers toward Misaki and has it pushed firmly back. Under the eaves, you sit in a row, shoulder to shoulder.
strings.毯子先给老人、孩子和湿透的人，我们在屋檐下守着过夜: Blankets go to the old, the children and the soaked first; we keep watch under the eaves through the night
strings.水产加工厂的中国技能实习生: Chinese technical intern at the fish-processing plant
strings.水从窗户和楼梯同时灌进来。{actor} 没能爬上屋顶。: Water pours in through the windows and up the stairs at once. {actor} doesn’t make it onto the roof.
strings.水喂下去了，可房梁纹丝不动。: The water is down, but the beam doesn’t move an inch.
strings.水喂下去了，房梁也撬开了，可阿部的心跳还是停了。: The water is down and the beam comes up, but Abe’s heart stops anyway.
strings.水喂下去了，房梁却撬不动。阿部喘着气说：“喝饱了，再等等也行。”: The water is down, but the beam won’t move. Abe pants, “I’ve had my fill. I can wait a bit longer.”
strings.水漫过楼顶栏杆的时候，{actor} 抓着的那截栏杆断了。: As the water pours over the roof railings, the section of railing {actor} is holding snaps.
strings.水退下去以后，活着的人踩着齐膝的泥水和瓦砾，在天黑前爬上了八幡神社。: When the water drains away, the living wade through knee-deep mud and rubble and reach the Hachiman Shrine before dark.
strings.求大家：现在就把墙撬开: Beg them to pry the wall off now
strings.汪！汪！（它冲着瓦砾堆叫了两声，回头看人。）: Woof! Woof! (He barks twice at the rubble and looks back at the people.)
strings.没事儿，大丈夫。咱东港人，冻不坏。: It’s fine, daijobu. We Donggang folks don’t freeze that easy.
strings.没有人去动那堵墙。{protagonist} 盯着天，过了很久才说：“好，我等。: No one touches the wall. {protagonist} stares at the sky, and it is a long time before {protagonist.he} says, “All right. I’ll wait.”
strings.没有人听得见 {actor} 在喊什么。混乱里，一个老人在石阶上被挤倒了，再也没: No one can hear what {actor} is shouting. In the crush, one of the old people is knocked down on the stone steps and never gets up.
strings.没有人回头。你们顺着神社的石阶一口气跑上了山顶。十几分钟后，海啸来了。: No one looks back. You run straight up the shrine steps to the top of the hill. Ten-odd minutes later, the tsunami comes.
strings.没有人探过这条路。走到半路，林道被塌方截断，队伍在雪地里绕了大半夜。: No one has scouted the route. Halfway along, the logging road is cut by a landslide, and the column wanders through the snow for most of the night.
strings.没有水和吃的，后面几天熬不过去；抢东西的人会被困在火里: Without food and water you won’t last the days ahead; but whoever goes in after them may be trapped by the fire
strings.没有药，只能熬着，等直升机: No medicine: hold on and wait for a helicopter
strings.没有药，至少别让他们再冻着、渴着: No medicine, but at least they won’t be cold and thirsty as well
strings.治伤口感染和肺炎的药。山上一片也没有。: Medicine for wound infections and pneumonia. There is not a single tablet on the hill.
strings.津波てんでんこ——各自跑；可他们不熟悉这里: “Tsunami tendenko”—everyone runs on their own; but they don’t know this place
strings.活着回去，而且没人知道你从小卖部拿了东西: Get home alive without anyone finding out what you took from the kiosk
strings.派一个人陪他下去，天亮以前回来: Send someone down with him, back before dawn
strings.派一个人陪她翻山: Send someone over the mountains with her
strings.派两个认路的人走出去报信，带救援队回来: Send two people who know the way to get word out and bring rescuers back
strings.派人冲下去喊他们回来: Send someone running down to call them back
