strings.浪头追上了石阶，{actor} 被拍倒在台阶上，呛了好几口黑水，是后面的人把 {: The wave reaches the steps and slams {actor} down onto them; {actor.he} swallows mouthfuls of black water before the people behind drag {actor.him} up.
strings.海啸里呛进去的海水和淤泥会引起吸入性肺炎（“海啸肺”），往往一两天后才发作；被瓦: Seawater and sludge swallowed in the tsunami cause aspiration pneumonia (“tsunami lung”), often a day or two later; wounds from the rubble pick up sludge and are 60% more likely than usual to become infected. Without antibiotics, both get deadlier by the day. For someone pinned for hours, simply lifting the weight off can trigger crush syndrome; getting fluids into them first lowers the risk.
strings.海水退下去的时候，你在二楼的窗口看见了：港口的海底露了出来，渔船歪在泥里。你知道: When the sea pulled back, you saw it from a second-floor window: the floor of the harbour laid bare, fishing boats tilted in the mud. You knew what it meant, but you held up your phone and filmed for almost a minute before you shouted the first “Run!” The video is still on your phone.
strings.海湾对面的灯一盏都没亮……没事的，那边停电了而已。: Not one light on across the bay… It’s fine. The power’s just out over there.
strings.海边的两层研修中心，背后是一座三十米高的小山，山顶有八幡神社和町里的防灾仓库；三: A two-story training centre by the sea, with a thirty-metre hill behind it crowned by the Hachiman Shrine and the town’s emergency supply shed; three hundred metres away stands the three-story Shiomi Elementary School.
strings.海退得那么远，我活了七十八年，只见过一回。: The sea went out that far once before in seventy-eight years. Once.
strings.消息传回来了：各个避难所的名单上，都没有小野寺由美。: The word comes back: Onodera Yumi is on none of the shelters’ lists.
strings.消防救援站的老班长: Veteran squad leader at a fire-rescue station
strings.清理遗物的时候，人们在 {actor} 的背包里发现了没拆封的饼干和巧克力。没有: When {actor.his} effects were cleared, people found unopened biscuits and chocolate in {actor}’s backpack. No one said anything. The biscuits were later placed on the offering table at the Hachiman Shrine.
strings.清酒被倒进了一个干净的瓶子里，和纱布放在了一起。: The sake is poured into a clean bottle and put away with the gauze.
strings.渡边老人养的柴犬，红棕色，卷尾巴，六岁，个头比一般的柴犬大一圈。平时跟着老人去港: Old Watanabe’s shiba inu: red coat, curly tail, six years old and a size bigger than most shibas. He usually follows the old man down to the harbour to look at the boats, and chases every seagull he sees. When the quake hit, he was lying under the lectern at the training centre.
strings.渡边老人喊了两声，小太郎又叫了一阵，才夹着尾巴跑了回来。: Watanabe calls him twice. Kotaro barks a while longer before he comes back, tail between his legs.
strings.渡边老人回来了，一句话也没说，在火堆边坐下，把一块烧焦的门牌放在了膝盖上。: Watanabe comes back without a word, sits down by the fire and lays a charred nameplate across his knees.
strings.渡边老人回来了，背上背着一个浑身是泥的老太太。他把她放在火边，自己坐在雪地里喘了: Watanabe comes back with a mud-caked old woman on his back. He lays her down by the fire, then sits in the snow, gasping, for a long time.
strings.渡边老人折了一根松枝，在篝火上点着，递了过来。: Watanabe snaps off a pine branch, lights it in the campfire and holds it out.
strings.渡边老人没有跟来。他骂了一句，拉着小太郎，一个人往八幡神社的石阶跑了。: Watanabe doesn’t come with you. He curses, pulls Kotaro along and runs for the Hachiman Shrine steps alone.
strings.渡边老人没能等到路通的那一天。镇上的人把他葬在了八幡神社下面能看见海的那块坡地上: Old Watanabe did not live to see the road open. The townspeople buried him on the slope below the Hachiman Shrine where you can see the sea. There is no inscription on the grave, only an old fish basket—he used to say a fisherman’s grave needs no name; the sea knows who he was.
strings.渡边老人蹲下来，让小太郎闻了闻葵的围巾。: Watanabe crouches down and lets Kotaro sniff Aoi’s scarf.
strings.渡边老人骂了一句“傻瓜”，拉着小太郎自己往山上跑了。: Watanabe curses—“Fools!”—and runs for the hill on his own, pulling Kotaro along.
strings.潮见小学三年级的学生。地震时她刚放学，正在回家的路上。妈妈在港口的水产加工厂上班: A third-grader at Shiomi Elementary School. When the quake hit, school had just let out and she was walking home. Her mother works at the fish-processing plant by the harbour and her father drives long-haul trucks out of Sendai. Her mother taught her: when a tsunami comes, don’t wait for Mum; run to the shrine on your own.
strings.潮见町后来的灾情报告里有一行小字：八幡神社避难所，在山上死亡 {var.crow: Shiomi’s later disaster report has a line in small print: Hachiman Shrine shelter, deaths on the hill: {var.crowd_dead}. {actor} photocopied that page and kept it in the little notebook, which lists the name of everyone on the hill and where each of them went afterwards.
strings.潮见高中二年级学生，想考护理学校，放学后和周末在研修中心当志愿者。今天她负责给考: A second-year student at Shiomi High School who wants to go to nursing school; she volunteers at the training centre after school and on weekends. Today she was handing out the trainees’ number cards and bringing them water. Her family lives in the fishing village across the bay: her father farms oysters and her mother works at the fishermen’s cooperative.
strings.火光里，锹和锯一刻也没有停。: In the firelight, the shovels and saws never stop for a moment.
strings.火堆边多了一个专门搓手的雪堆。: A pile of snow appears by the fire, just for scrubbing hands.
strings.火堆边，一个浑身湿透的老渔民在说：“我老伴儿听了广播，说浪才三米，就在二楼收衣服: By the fire, an old fisherman soaked to the skin is saying, “My wife heard the radio say the wave would only be three metres, so she was upstairs bringing in the washing…” He can’t go on. {actor} remembers the words {actor.he} repeated so loudly after the quake, “expected wave height: three metres,” and the line that came after: “Two floors. We’re fine.”
strings.火堆边，几个镇民压低了声音：听说夜里有外国人在瓦砾里偷东西，翻死人的口袋。说着，: By the fire, a few townspeople lower their voices: they’ve heard that foreigners are stealing from the rubble at night, going through the pockets of the dead. As they talk, someone glances at the corner where the interns are sitting. Lina Sun goes white.
strings.火已经烧到了半山腰。杉树一棵接一棵地烧成火炬，热浪顺着石阶往上涌，神社的屋檐上落: The fire has reached halfway up the hill. One cedar after another goes up like a torch; waves of heat surge up the stone steps, and sparks shower onto the shrine’s eaves. The townspeople start crowding toward the back of the hill.
strings.火点小的时候最好扑；可下去的人离火最近: Spot fires are easiest to beat while they’re small, but whoever goes down is closest to the flames
strings.火点扑灭了一半，风一吹又着了。{actor} 的手被烫起了泡。: Half the spot fires are out when a gust of wind sets them going again. {actor}’s hands come up in blisters.
strings.火烧上山时被浓烟呛死: Choked by smoke when the fire took the hilltop
strings.火烧进了山坡上的杉树林。站在石阶顶上，能看见火线一点一点往上爬。: The fire has got into the cedar woods on the slope. From the top of the steps you can watch the line of flame creep upward.
strings.火烧进山坡的程度，100 = 烧到了神社。: How far the fire has climbed the slope; 100 means it has reached the shrine.
strings.火翻上了山顶。社务所的屋檐先着了，接着是仓库的木门。浓烟里，有人在喊孩子的名字。: The fire comes over the top of the hill. The eaves of the shrine office catch first, then the wooden door of the shed. In the thick smoke, someone is calling a child’s name.
strings.火边腾出了一块地方。千代奶奶捧着热水，过了很久才说出一句：“孩子……谢谢。”: They make room by the fire. Granny Chiyo cradles the hot water, and it is a long time before she manages to say, “Child… thank you.”
strings.点名的事说出来以后，千代奶奶只说了一句：“千叶那孩子要是知道，最后是你一直推着我: After the head count came out, Granny Chiyo said only one thing: “If Chiba knew it was you who kept pushing me all the way, she’d be glad.” Every spring after that, {actor} visited her at the inland nursing home and wheeled her once around the garden. The year she turned ninety, Granny Chiyo had someone write a line on a card for her: “Chiba was not your fault.”
strings.热心、急性子，习惯冲在最前面，也习惯替别人拿主意；最怕被人看见自己犹豫。: Warm-hearted and impatient, used to charging in first and to deciding for others; what he fears most is being seen to hesitate.
strings.热心、爱张罗，天生会安排人；嘴上总说“大家听我说”，心里其实最怕自己安排错了。: Warm and bustling, a born organizer of people; she’s always saying “Listen, everyone,” but what she fears most is organizing it wrong.
strings.热心、胆子大，什么都抢着干；一停下来就会想家，所以不肯停下来。: Warm-hearted and bold, she grabs every job going; whenever she stops, she starts thinking about home, so she doesn’t stop.
strings.爸爸开的大卡车，能开到山上来吗？: Can Dad’s big truck drive up the hill?
strings.爸爸的船昨天刚刷过漆。: Dad painted his boat just yesterday.
strings.爽快、能扛事，说话带着东北人的幽默，不喜欢别人可怜她。心里一直算着两笔账：一笔是: Frank and tough, with a northeasterner’s sense of humour, and she doesn’t like being pitied. She keeps two accounts in her head: her little brother’s school fees back home, and every one of the nineteen at the plant.
strings.狗不会无缘无故地叫: A dog doesn’t bark for nothing
strings.狗鼻子比人灵；可小太郎只听渡边老人的: A dog’s nose beats a person’s; but Kotaro only listens to Watanabe
strings.现在别听：她承受不住坏消息: Don’t listen now: she couldn’t bear bad news
strings.现在就下去：顺着屋顶摸过去，把人接出来: Go down now: feel your way across the rooftops and bring them out
strings.现在就开防火带：能动的人拿上锹和锯，下去砍出一条隔离带: Cut a firebreak now: everyone who can move takes a shovel or a saw and goes down to clear a strip
strings.现在就撬开，趁压得还不久: Pry it off now, before it’s been too long
strings.现在搬不动：给他留下水和毯子，做好记号，等自卫队带着工具和输液来: We can’t move it now: leave him water and a blanket, mark the spot and wait for the SDF with tools and IV drips
strings.瓦砾底下，传来了微弱的敲击声。: From under the rubble comes a faint knocking.
strings.瓦砾里的煤气罐、汽车和油罐烧起来的火。夜里会蔓延，风越大烧得越快，雨雪能压住一些: Gas cylinders, cars and oil tanks burning in the rubble. It spreads at night, faster in the wind; rain and snow damp it down a little.
strings.用仓库里的蓝色防水布、竹竿和瓦砾里的木头，在社务所背风的一侧搭一个棚子，挡住风雪: Put up a shelter on the lee side of the shrine office with blue tarps from the shed, bamboo poles and wood from the rubble, to keep out the wind and snow. With cardboard and cushions laid underneath, people can actually sleep in it.
strings.用掉 2 升水；先补水，搬开时的风险小得多: Uses 2 L of water; with fluids in first, the moment of release is far less dangerous
strings.用门板盖好，插一根竹竿做记号: Cover him with the door again and mark the spot with a bamboo pole
strings.用防水布、竹竿和木头，在社务所背风的一侧搭一个棚子。棚子搭起来以前，你们几个只能: Put up a shelter of tarps, bamboo poles and timber on the lee side of the shrine office. Until it’s up, you can only huddle under the drafty eaves at night.
strings.电台修好了，天线也重新竖了起来，可没有电。得在瓦砾里找到一块汽车电瓶。: The radio is fixed and the antenna is back up, but there is no power. Someone has to find a car battery in the rubble.
strings.电瓶接上了。防灾无线电台的指示灯亮了，喇叭里沙沙响了一阵，传出一个人声：“这里是: The battery is connected. The disaster radio’s indicator light comes on; the speaker hisses for a while, then a human voice: “This is the town disaster headquarters. Hachiman Shrine, please respond!”
strings.电话通了。{actor} 只说了一句“我还活着”，那边就哭了起来。没说几句，信号: The call goes through. {actor} gets out only “I’m alive” before the other end starts to cry. A few words more, and the signal drops.
strings.电话通了二十秒。{actor} 一口气报出了人数、伤员和位置。对面说：“记下了，: The call holds for twenty seconds. In one breath {actor} reels off the head count, the injuries and the location. The voice at the other end says, “Got it. Hachiman Shrine.” Then the signal is gone.
strings.留下来最稳妥；可有人会不听，自己走: Staying is safest; but some won’t listen and will go on their own
strings.留着当消毒酒精，给伤口清创用: Save it as disinfectant for cleaning wounds
strings.疏散的时候，你负责点名。点到一半你就知道少了一个人——养老院的护工千叶，她把千代: During the evacuation you were in charge of the head count. Halfway through you knew one person was missing—Chiba, the nursing-home caregiver, who had pushed Granny Chiyo over to your group and run back for another resident. You called out “Everyone’s here,” because you were afraid someone would go back for her.
strings.病人被挪到了篝火边，一口一口地喝着热水。: The sick are moved up beside the campfire, sipping hot water.
strings.直升机和后来的车，一趟一趟地把人从山上接走。每一趟，都有人留在下面，看着它走远。: The helicopters, and later the trucks, took people off the hill trip after trip. Each time, someone was left behind, watching it go. Those who were taken out: {survivors}. Those who didn’t live to see their turn: {dead}. No one ever cleared away the SOS on the open ground in front of the Hachiman Shrine. Long afterwards, when the snow had melted, the three white letters were still lying there.
strings.直升机拔地而起，往内陆的方向飞去了。: The helicopter lifts off and heads inland.
strings.直升机来过几趟。: How many times the helicopter has come.
strings.直接撬开拿：人命要紧: Just pry it open: lives come first
strings.相信他们：听到警报，他们会自己往高处跑: Trust them: when they hear the siren, they’ll run for high ground on their own
strings.短句多，常用医学词：“先止血。”“他还有意识吗？”“别让他睡过去。”: Short sentences, lots of medical words: “Stop the bleeding first.” “Is he conscious?” “Don’t let him fall asleep.”
strings.石阶下面倒着一台自动售货机，玻璃碎了一半，里面还立着几十瓶茶和矿泉水。旁边那家酒: A vending machine lies toppled at the bottom of the stone steps, its glass half smashed, dozens of bottles of tea and water still standing inside. The owner of the liquor shop next door squats on the rubble in his doorway, smoking and watching you.
strings.研修班的结业证书是三个月后寄出的，日期写着那个星期五。{actor} 的那一份，: The course certificates were sent out three months later, dated that Friday. {actor}’s came back to the course office, where it stayed in a drawer no one ever opened.
strings.碎玻璃划破了手: Cut a hand on broken glass
strings.社务所的柜子里有几瓶祭祀用的清酒。几个冻得发抖的渔民提议：一人喝一口，暖暖身子。: In a cupboard in the shrine office are a few bottles of ceremonial sake. Some of the fishermen, shivering with cold, suggest a mouthful each to warm up.
strings.神社前的台阶上，有人开始一个一个地登记名字。: On the steps in front of the shrine, someone starts registering names, one by one.
strings.神社手水舍的水是从后山一眼山泉用竹管引下来的，地震把竹管和水管震断了。顺着管子往: The shrine’s purification fountain is fed by a mountain spring behind the hill through bamboo pipes, and the quake snapped the pipes and hoses. Follow them up into the woods and join them back section by section, and there will be a steady stream of water.
strings.神社的两条长幡挂上了鸟居，下面一股浓烟笔直地升了起来。: The shrine’s two long banners go up on the torii, and beneath them a column of thick smoke rises straight into the sky.
strings.神社的钟“当、当、当”地响了起来，一声接一声。: The shrine bell starts to ring—dong, dong, dong—stroke after stroke.
strings.神社的钟响了起来。: The shrine bell begins to ring.
strings.神社里能烧的木头: Wood at the shrine that will burn
strings.离核电站越远越安心；可在雪地里抬着担架走十八公里，最先倒下的会是老人: The farther from the plant, the safer you’ll feel; but carry stretchers eighteen kilometres through the snow and the old will be the first to drop
strings.离火最近的活；开得出来，神社就保住了: The job nearest the fire; finish it and the shrine is saved
strings.私下凑过去，要一块: Sidle over quietly and ask for a piece
strings.站出来稳住大家：这里海拔三十米，浪上不来: Step up and calm everyone: we’re thirty metres up, the waves can’t reach us
strings.站出来说话：我们也是外国人，谁看见了，当面说清楚: Speak up: we’re foreigners too—if anyone saw something, say it to our faces
strings.第{day}天，推土机在瓦砾中间推出了一条路，自卫队的卡车开到了山脚下。带队的军: On day {day}, a bulldozer pushes a road through the rubble and SDF trucks reach the foot of the hill. The officer in charge climbs the stone steps and calls the roll, name by name: “Anyone who can walk rides the trucks to the shelters inland. Anyone who can’t, we carry down.”
strings.第一夜下雪，夜里零下三度上下。核心体温逐小时计算：湿透的衣服让体感温度再低六度；: It snows on the first night, around minus three degrees after dark. Core temperature is simulated hour by hour: soaked clothes make it feel six degrees colder, and wind, how drafty the shelter is, the campfire and the warmth of bodies huddled together all count. The old, the young, the injured and the hungry can shiver out less heat and are the first to become hypothermic. Getting out of wet clothes, lighting a fire and putting up a windbreak matter more than anything.
strings.第二天傍晚，翻山的队伍走进了内陆的町。自卫队的营地里有热汤和暖炉，可清点人数的时: Toward evening the next day, the column walks into the inland town. The SDF camp has hot soup and stoves, but when heads are counted, there are several fewer than set out.
strings.第二天，实习生们和镇民混在一起捡柴、烧水、照看老人。没有人再提那件事。: The next day the interns work side by side with the townspeople, gathering wood, boiling water and looking after the old. No one brings it up again.
strings.第二波比第一波大。天黑以前，谁也别下去。: The second wave is bigger than the first. Nobody goes down before dark.
strings.第五天，推土机终于在瓦砾中间推出了一条路，自卫队的卡车一辆接一辆地开到了山脚下。: On the fifth day, the bulldozers finally push a road through the rubble, and Self-Defense Forces trucks pull up at the foot of the hill one after another.
strings.等出去了，我请你们喝酒。……酒馆大概也没了。: When we’re out of here, the drinks are on me. …Though the bar’s probably gone too.
strings.等天亮退潮了再去: Wait for daylight and the ebb tide
strings.等救援最稳妥；可救援什么时候来，谁也说不准: Waiting for rescue is safest; but no one can say when it will come
strings.等救援来了再说；可她每天都在问: Wait until rescue comes; but she asks every day
strings.等救援队带着输液和液压顶杆来，最稳妥；可他还能熬多久，谁也说不准: Waiting for the rescuers with IV drips and hydraulic jacks is the safest course; but how long he can hold out, no one can say
strings.等火势过去，大家才在后山的背风坡上一个一个地找人。: Only when the fire has passed do they start searching the lee slope behind the hill for each other, one person at a time.
strings.等火势过去，所有人都挤在后山的背风坡上。神社只剩下几根冒烟的黑柱子。: When the fire has passed, everyone is huddled on the lee slope behind the hill. Of the shrine, only a few smoking black pillars remain.
strings.等路通了，我请你们吃潮见的海胆。……要是还有海胆的话。: When the road’s open I’ll treat you all to Shiomi sea urchin. …If there’s any sea urchin left.
strings.粗声粗气，爱自嘲：“这根梁子，比我老婆还沉。”: Gruff, self-mocking: “This beam’s heavier than my wife.”
strings.纸一着就卷了起来，那一栏字在火里亮了一下，就没了。: The paper curls the moment it catches; the words in that box glow for an instant in the flames, and are gone.
strings.组织镇民，用桶装雪，浇湿神社周围的地面和屋檐: Organize the townspeople to fill buckets with snow and soak the ground and eaves around the shrine
strings.结业考核的那个下午，地震来了。这一次，没有人会喊“推演结束”。: The afternoon of the final assessment, the earthquake came. This time, no one is going to call “end of simulation.”
strings.结算用的临时计数。: A temporary count used during resolution.
strings.绕过火场，走到两公里外的镇公所和诊所：那里可能有药、有吃的、有汽车电瓶，还能把山: Skirt the fires and walk two kilometres to the town hall and the clinic: there may be medicine, food and a car battery there, and you can report the situation on the hill to the town disaster headquarters. You will spend a night in the ruins and won’t be back for twelve hours, and aftershocks and tsunami warnings can catch you on the way.
strings.给仓库里的老人用，开着门: Give it to the old people in the shed, with the door open
strings.给他送去热水和毯子，陪他说说话，再等等: Take him hot water and a blanket, keep him company and wait a little longer
strings.给她和孩子一份，别的人顾不过来: Give her and the child a share; you can’t look after everyone
strings.给山上的镇民登记名字、分组，照看老人和孩子，把湿衣服换下来烤干，安排人轮流捡柴、: Register the townspeople on the hill and divide them into groups, look after the old and the children, get wet clothes off and dried, and set up rotas for wood and water. Organized townspeople will help with the work, and fewer of them will freeze or fall sick and die.
strings.给我口水喝就行，别的不要。: Just give me a sip of water. I don’t need anything else.
strings.给老人们每人一小口，让他们睡得着: Give each of the old people a small sip so they can sleep
strings.绳子在黑暗里甩了一次又一次。: Again and again, the rope is flung out into the dark.
strings.绳子够不着。喊了很久，那边没有回答。: The rope won’t reach. You shout for a long time, but no answer comes.
strings.罐头被悄悄藏在了避风棚的防水布底下。孙丽娜看着那堆箱子，一句话也没说。: The cans are quietly hidden under the tarp of the windbreak shelter. Lina Sun looks at the stack of cases and says nothing.
strings.美咲一个人推着千代奶奶的轮椅，最后一个冲上了石阶。两个人的腿都泡了水，浑身发抖。: Misaki pushes Granny Chiyo’s wheelchair up the steps alone, the last ones to make it. Both of them are wet to the knees and shaking.
strings.美咲后来考上了仙台的护理学校。入学典礼那天，她给 {actor} 寄来一张照片，: Misaki later got into a nursing school in Sendai. On the day of the entrance ceremony she sent {actor} a photo with a note on the back: “The person who ran past me that day never left anyone behind on the hill afterwards. Those later days are what I remember.” {actor} slipped the photo inside the course certificate that arrived three months late.
strings.美咲回来了。她说渔村的公民馆里有名单，名单上没有她爸爸妈妈。说完，她拿起柴刀，又: Misaki comes back. She says there was a list at the village community hall, and her parents weren’t on it. Then she picks up the hatchet and goes back to gathering firewood.
strings.美咲回来了，什么也没说。: Misaki comes back and says nothing.
strings.美咲回来了，眼睛是肿的，嘴角却是笑着的：爸爸妈妈都在渔村的公民馆里，牡蛎筏子全没: Misaki comes back with swollen eyes but a smile at the corners of her mouth: her mother and father are both at the village community hall, and the oyster rafts are all gone. She says, too, that the logging road behind the hill goes right over the ridge.
strings.美咲回来了：爸爸妈妈都活着，在渔村的公民馆里。翻山的林道，她认得了。: Misaki is back: her parents are both alive, at the village community hall. And she knows the logging road over the mountains now.
strings.美咲在内陆的亲戚家住了半年，一直在避难所的名单上找爸爸妈妈的名字。她还是考上了护: Misaki lived with relatives inland for six months, searching the shelter lists for her parents’ names. She still got into nursing school. In the “reason for applying” box on her application she wrote one sentence: “That day on the hill, I didn’t know how to do anything.”
strings.美咲愣了一下，低头看着杯子里的热水。过了很久，她说：“谢谢你告诉我。”: Misaki goes still and looks down at the hot water in her cup. After a long time she says, “Thank you for telling me.”
strings.美咲没能走下那座山。她的号码牌后来在神社的石阶上被人捡到，正面写着“志愿者 高桥: Misaki never made it down from the hill. Her number card was later found on the shrine steps, with “Volunteer Takahashi” on the front and a tiny nurse’s cap drawn in ballpoint on the back.
strings.美咲点点头，又拿起了望远镜。: Misaki nods and picks up the binoculars again.
strings.美咲用捡来的望远镜看了很久海湾对面。她家所在的渔村只剩几栋白色的房子立在山坡上，: Misaki looks across the bay for a long time through a pair of binoculars she found. Of the fishing village where her family lives, only a few white houses still stand on the hillside, and the bridge that led there is down. “I’ll take the mountain paths. Two mountains—I can be there before dark tomorrow.”
strings.美咲的爸爸妈妈都活了下来，牡蛎筏子全没了。她第二年考上了仙台的护理学校，毕业后回: Misaki’s mother and father both survived; the oyster rafts were all gone. The next year she got into nursing school in Sendai, and after graduating she came back to Shiomi to work as a nurse in a clinic in the temporary prefabs. On the clinic wall hangs a handwritten notice: “Earthquake? Run for high ground first. Don’t wait for anyone.”
strings.美咲给 {actor} 递过来一杯热水，突然说：“地震那会儿，我在走廊里被柜子绊: Misaki hands {actor} a cup of hot water and says out of nowhere, “When the quake hit, I tripped over a cabinet in the corridor and called out, and someone ran right past me. I didn’t see who it was.” She smiles. “I don’t blame them. In their place, I’d have run too.”
strings.美咲背上一瓶水和两个饭团，向大家鞠了一躬，钻进了后山的林道。: Misaki takes a bottle of water and two rice balls, bows to everyone and disappears up the logging road behind the hill.
strings.翻了半天，只翻出淤泥和湿透的棉被: Hours of digging turned up nothing but sludge and sodden quilts
strings.翻山的路上，{actor} 在担架上慢慢没了声音。抬担架的人走出好远才发现。: On the way over the mountain, {actor} slowly falls silent on the stretcher. The bearers have walked a long way before anyone notices.
strings.翻山的路上，美咲在一段结了冰的塌方上滑了下去。: On the way over the mountain, Misaki slips on a frozen landslide and slides away.
strings.翻山那天，千代奶奶在担架上冻得说不出话，可她活了下来。后来她常说，那一路上抬担架: On the day they crossed the mountain, Granny Chiyo was so frozen on her stretcher she couldn’t speak, but she lived. She often said afterwards that the stretcher-bearers changed a dozen times along the way and she remembered every one of them: “I owe a dozen people. I have to live till I’ve paid them all back.” She lived to ninety.
strings.老人们围着暖炉坐成一圈，有人把冻僵的手伸了过去。: The old folks sit in a ring around the heater, and someone holds out a pair of frozen hands to it.
strings.老人在石阶上站了很久，最后把竹竿往地上一戳，转身回到火堆边，一整夜没有再说话。: The old man stands on the steps for a long time, then jabs his pole into the ground, turns back to the fire and says nothing more all night.
strings.老人点点头，没再回头。雨衣和小太郎卷着的尾巴，很快就看不见了。: The old man nods and doesn’t look back. Soon the raincoat and Kotaro’s curled tail are lost from sight.
strings.老人看完，沉默了很久，把手机还给 {actor}：“谢谢。后来的人用得上。”旁边: The old man watches it through and is silent for a long time. He hands the phone back to {actor}. “Thank you. The people who come after us will need this.” For a while, no one who saw the screen says a word.
strings.老人被一个一个背到了后山的背风坡上，裹着毯子缩成一团。没有人睡得着。: One by one the old people are carried to the lee slope behind the hill, where they huddle in blankets. No one can sleep.
strings.老人被一个一个背到了后山，物资堆在一块大石头后面。: One by one the old people are carried to the back of the hill, and the supplies are piled behind a big rock.
strings.老伴儿的名字后来出现在失踪者名单上，一直没有找到。渡边住进了内陆的临时板房，屋里: His wife’s name later appeared on the list of the missing, and she was never found. Watanabe moved into a temporary prefab inland, with nothing on the walls but an old photo and a big-catch banner. Every March the schools invited him to talk about the tsunami; he said one sentence and sat down: “When the sea pulls back, run. Don’t look back.”
strings.老伴儿腿上的伤养了一个春天。渡边后来再也没有出过海，船早就没了。他每天早上牵着小: The injury to his wife’s leg took a whole spring to heal. Watanabe never went to sea again; his boat was long gone. Every morning he walked Kotaro up the steps of the Hachiman Shrine and stood at the top for a while, looking at the sea. When people asked what he was looking at, he said, “Whether it’s pulling back again.”
strings.老板摆摆手：“拿吧拿吧，都拿走。反正也卖不了了。”他把烟掐了，过来帮着搬。: The owner waves a hand. “Take them, take them—take the lot. I can’t sell them now anyway.” He stubs out his cigarette and comes over to help carry.
strings.老林业工人的办法，弄好了能一下子截住火；弄不好，就是自己放火烧山: An old forester’s trick: done right, it stops the fire at a stroke; done wrong, you’ve set the hill on fire yourselves
strings.老渔民们抿了一口，眯着眼睛说起了年轻时出海的事。: The old fishermen take a sip and, eyes half closed, start telling stories of going to sea when they were young.
strings.老渔民看着 {actor}，很久没有说话，最后摇了摇头：“广播是那么说的，不怪你: The old fisherman looks at {actor} for a long time without a word, and at last shakes his head. “That’s what the radio said. It’s not your fault.”
strings.考官回不来了，就自己写: The examiner isn’t coming back, so write it yourselves
strings.能多救几十个人。投这个选项的人去喊人，会是最后一批上山的: It could save dozens. Whoever votes for this goes to warn them and will be among the last up the hill
strings.能忍、爱开玩笑，疼的时候就骂自己。说起女儿就停不下来。: Tough, a joker, curses himself when it hurts. Once he starts talking about his daughter he can’t stop.
strings.能拆的都拆了，剩下的只有石头和那几棵神木: Everything that could come apart has—only stone and the sacred trees are left
strings.能拖一阵子；挡不挡得住，要看风: It buys some time; whether it holds depends on the wind
strings.能躲开风雪；可社务所只有那么大，有几个老人只能挪到门口去: Out of the wind and snow; but the office is only so big, and some of the old people will have to move to the doorway
strings.脱下自己的外套给她裹上: Take off your own coat and wrap her in it
strings.腿？早就没感觉了。没感觉好，不疼。: My legs? Lost the feeling ages ago. That’s good—no feeling, no pain.
strings.自卫队员先给压在墙下的 {actor} 输上了液，再用液压顶杆撑开了墙。: The troops first get an IV drip into {actor}, still pinned under the wall, then jack the wall up off {actor.him}.
strings.自卫队员挨个给老人量体温、喂热水。: The troops go from one old person to the next, taking temperatures and giving them hot water to drink.
strings.自卫队员背着输液袋和液压顶杆，跟着你们下了山。: The troops shoulder IV bags and a hydraulic jack and follow you down the hill.
strings.至少让大家饭前用雪搓手，病人用的碗单独放: At least have everyone scrub their hands with snow before eating, and keep the sick people’s bowls apart
strings.药店废墟里的一盒纱布和消毒水: A box of gauze and disinfectant from the ruined pharmacy
strings.药店柜台底下找到的一盒抗生素: A box of antibiotics found under the pharmacy counter
strings.葵一直坐在火堆边，把书包抱在怀里。谁跟她说话她都点头，可一句话也不说，夜里醒过来: Aoi sits by the fire with her school bag in her arms. She nods at anyone who speaks to her but never says a word, and when she wakes in the night she looks over toward the stone steps. Granny Chiyo says, “This child needs a grown-up with her all the time.” Choose someone to look after Aoi.
strings.葵没能走下那座山。她的红书包后来被送进了潮见町的震灾资料馆，里面有一本作业本，最: Aoi never made it down from the hill. Her red school bag went to Shiomi’s earthquake archive. Inside is a notebook whose last page carries the title of the essay due the next day: “My Mum.”
strings.葵的妈妈一直没有找到。爸爸从仙台赶来，在避难所的名单前站了很久。葵跟着爸爸搬去了: Aoi’s mother was never found. Her father came from Sendai and stood in front of the shelter lists for a long time. Aoi moved to Sendai with him, still carrying the same red school bag. Years later she became a primary school teacher, and every March she took her pupils up the hill behind the school, counting the steps as they climbed.
strings.葵的妈妈是从水产厂冷库的楼顶被直升机救下来的，冻掉了两个脚趾。母女俩在内陆中学的: Aoi’s mother had been lifted by helicopter from the roof of the plant’s cold store and lost two toes to frostbite. When mother and daughter met in the gym of the inland junior high, Aoi didn’t cry; she just held on to the hem of her mother’s jacket, all night long. In junior high she wrote in an essay: “Mum told me not to wait for her, and I didn’t. Mum says she didn’t wait for me either. We both did the right thing.”
strings.蓝色的防水布绷了起来，四角压着瓦砾里捡来的木头。棚子底下铺了一层纸板和神社的坐垫: The blue tarp goes taut, its corners weighed down with timber from the rubble. Under it, a layer of cardboard and the shrine’s floor cushions; the wind drops at once.
strings.螺旋桨的声音由远及近——一架自卫队的直升机看见了山顶的 SOS，在神社前的空地上: The thud of rotors grows closer—a Self-Defense Forces helicopter has spotted the SOS on the hilltop and comes to a hover over the open ground in front of the shrine, kicking up a cloud of snow. A crewman jumps down and shouts, “Four at a time, no more! Injured and sick first! The next trip is hours away!”
strings.街道应急办的副主任: Deputy head of a neighbourhood emergency office
strings.被压在瓦砾里的阿部还撑得住多久。: How much longer Abe can hold out, pinned in the rubble.
strings.被墙压住腿的人已经被压了多少个小时。: How many hours the person with legs trapped under a wall has been pinned.
strings.被钉子和碎玻璃划伤: cut by nails and broken glass
strings.西风刮得人站不稳，火星子被吹得满天飞。: A west wind strong enough to knock you off balance, sparks flying everywhere.
strings.要撤去哪儿？别把我送得太远，我想死在潮见。: Evacuate where? Don’t send me too far. I want to die in Shiomi.
strings.要是有人从我身边跑过去，我也不怪他。真的。: If someone ran past me, I wouldn’t blame them. Really.
strings.警报一直没有解除，可总有人要下山——捡柴、找人、找药。活下来的：{survivo: The warning was never lifted, but someone always had to go down—for firewood, for people, for medicine. Those who lived: {survivors}. Those who stayed down there: {dead}. Shiomi later added one line to its disaster-preparedness handbook: A tsunami is never just one wave; until the warning is lifted, no one goes back down to low ground.
strings.警报响的时候，{actor} 还在瓦砾深处。这一次，水真的来了。: When the siren sounds, {actor} is still deep in the rubble. This time, the water really does come.
strings.警报响的时候，{actor} 还在离海最近的那片瓦砾里。: When the siren sounds, {actor} is still in the rubble nearest the sea.
strings.警报响的时候，{actor} 还在离海最近的那片瓦砾里。后来，那里只剩下一只背包: When the siren sounds, {actor} is still in the rubble nearest the sea. Afterwards, all that is left there is a backpack.
strings.让 {protagonist} 平躺、保暖，守着: Lay {protagonist} flat, keep {protagonist.him} warm and watch over {protagonist.him}
strings.让他平躺、保暖，守着他，等直升机: Lay him flat, keep him warm, watch over him and wait for a helicopter
strings.让他的家人以后找得到: So his family can find him later
strings.让他自己去。换了是我，我也会去: Let him go alone. I’d do the same in his place
strings.让外面的人知道山上有人。地上摆出 SOS，直升机才看得见；再点起烟、挂起旗更醒目: Letting the outside know there are people on the hill. A helicopter can only see an SOS laid out on the ground; smoke and banners make it stand out more; a working radio lets you talk to them directly. Snow covers the SOS.
strings.让她去——她有权知道家里人怎么样了: Let her go—she has a right to know what’s happened to her family
strings.让她心里好受一点: It will ease her mind a little
strings.让她跟车走——这是她们回家的车: Let her go with the bus—it’s their ride home
strings.让实习生们和我们、和镇民一起干活，所有人都看得见: Get the interns working alongside us and the townspeople, where everyone can see
strings.让湿透的人马上脱掉湿衣服，换上仓库里的运动服，大家挤在一起: Get the soaked ones out of their wet clothes right now and into the tracksuits from the shed, and everyone huddle together
strings.让铃木千代奶奶活着出去: Get Granny Suzuki Chiyo out alive
strings.让高桥美咲活着离开潮见: Get Takahashi Misaki out of Shiomi alive
strings.诊所药柜里的几盒抗生素: A few boxes of antibiotics from the clinic’s drug cabinet
strings.话少、倔，一辈子只信海和自己的眼睛。“津波てんでんこ”挂在嘴边：海啸来了各自跑，: Taciturn and stubborn; all his life he has trusted only the sea and his own eyes. “Tsunami tendenko” is never far from his lips: when a tsunami comes, everyone runs on their own—don’t look back, don’t wait for anyone. But what weighs on him most is his wife, at home by the harbour.
strings.语速平，爱用技术词：“信号”“电压”“先断电再接”。不太看人的眼睛。: Even-voiced, fond of technical words—“signal,” “voltage,” “cut the power before you connect.” Rarely looks people in the eye.
strings.语速快，爱说“我去！”“交给我！”；紧张的时候会小声念家里人的名字。: Talks fast, likes “I’ll go!” and “Leave it to me!”; when she’s tense she murmurs her family’s names under her breath.
strings.说一个自己的故事: Tell a story of your own
strings.说出来，大家都会好受一点: Telling it will make everyone feel a little better
strings.说出来，她也许会原谅；别人也会知道: Tell her and she may forgive you, but the others will know too
strings.说出来，心里也许会轻一点；所有人都会知道: Saying it may lighten the load, but everyone will know
strings.说她跟着别的老人去了小学: Say she went to the school with the other old folks
strings.说实话：她跑回去了，我喊的是“人齐了”: Tell the truth: she ran back, and I called out “Everyone’s here”
strings.说得对，大家就能安心睡一觉；说得不好，石阶上会出事: Get it right and everyone sleeps easy; get it wrong and someone gets hurt on the steps
strings.说话慢，句子短：“这条路能走。”“别急，先看。”: Speaks slowly, in short sentences: “This way is passable.” “Don’t rush. Look first.”
strings.请她留下来当翻译，等自卫队来了再走: Ask her to stay on as interpreter until the Self-Defense Forces come
strings.谣言当面戳破就没了；可说不好，会让火堆边的气氛更僵: Call a rumour out in the open and it dies, but handle it badly and the mood by the fire gets worse
strings.费柴、费人手；能把病挡在门外: Costs firewood and hands, but can keep the sickness out
strings.走廊里的事，{actor} 一直没说出口。美咲后来考上了护理学校，每年三月都寄来: {actor} never spoke about the corridor. Misaki got into nursing school, and every March she sent a card signed with a drawing of a curly-tailed shiba inu. {actor} always wrote back, and always wanted to add “I’m sorry” at the end, and always crossed it out.
strings.走的人背上了一半的水。留下的人站在石阶上，看着他们钻进了林子。: Those leaving take half the water. Those staying stand on the stone steps and watch them disappear into the woods.
strings.趁天亮下山找人：瓦砾底下一定还有活着的人: Go down and search for people while it’s light: there must still be people alive under the rubble
strings.跑得动的人能马上脱身；跑不动的人……: Those who can run get clear at once; those who can’t…
strings.跟他商量：东西拿上山，大家一起分，他家孩子先吃: Talk it over with him: take it up the hill and share it, and his children eat first
strings.跟她去冷库，能搬多少搬多少，分给山上所有人: Go to the cold store with her, carry back all you can and share it with everyone on the hill
strings.跟着它下去看看: Follow him down and take a look
strings.路通了再去最稳妥；可她每一个钟头都在想: Going once the road is open is safest; but every hour she thinks of nothing else
strings.路通了，可走下山的人，比爬上山的时候少了很多。活下来的：{survivors}。: The road opened, but far fewer walked down the hill than had climbed it. Those who lived: {survivors}. Those who stayed on that hill: {dead}. The course later sent a certificate to every trainee’s home, to the living and to those who never came back, not one left out. Many years later, the survivors still woke on snowy nights and felt their clothes to make sure they were dry.
strings.路通的那天，你们跟着最后一批镇民下了山。{survivors}——大多数人都活了: On the day the road opened, you came down the hill with the last of the townspeople. {survivors}—most of you made it out alive. Those who did not live to see this day: {dead}. As the trucks pulled out of Shiomi, someone looked back once at the shrine on the hilltop, then quickly turned away. In the back of the truck, the last half piece of hardtack went from hand to hand all the way round and came back to where it started.
strings.车上暖和，能直接开到内陆的医院: The bus is warm and can drive straight to a hospital inland
strings.车门关上的时候，山上没有人挥手。: When the doors close, no one on the hill waves.
strings.辽宁东港人，来潮见的水产加工厂当技能实习生一年半了，每天在冷库里切秋刀鱼、装罐头: From Donggang in Liaoning, she has spent a year and a half as a technical intern at the Shiomi fish-processing plant, cutting saury and canning fish in the cold store every day. Her Japanese is the best of the interns’, so this afternoon the plant lent her to the training centre to interpret for the assessment. Nineteen other young women came over with her and work at the plant.
strings.这一趟已经安排了几个人。: How many people have been given a place on this trip.
strings.这句话对她也对自己: Words for her, and for yourself
strings.这是他的家、他的老伴儿；可一个七十八岁的老人，在雪夜里走进火场边的瓦砾……: It’s his home, his wife; but a man of seventy-eight, walking into the rubble at the edge of the fire on a snowy night…
strings.这是官方的预报，大家都听见了；外面余震不断，乱跑反而危险。可万一不止三米……: It’s the official forecast, and everyone heard it; with aftershocks still coming, running around outside could be worse. But if it’s more than three metres…
strings.这是那个下午留下来的东西: It’s what’s left of that afternoon
strings.这根梁子，比我老婆还沉。: This beam’s heavier than my wife.
strings.这种时候，东西在谁手里就是谁的: At a time like this, it belongs to whoever’s holding it
strings.这种时候，谁都有自己的难处: At a time like this, everyone has their own troubles
strings.这雪下得好。雪压得住火。: Good, this snow. Snow keeps the fire down.
strings.这雪会停的。天一亮就停。: The snow will stop. It stops at first light.
strings.迪庆香格里拉人，在雪山脚下长大，当了九年登山向导，后来加入了一支民间山地救援队。: From Shangri-La in Diqing, she grew up at the foot of snow mountains, worked nine years as a mountain guide, then joined a volunteer mountain rescue team. She joined the course to learn how to organize post-disaster search and rescue. She says little, walks lightly and knows a route like the back of her hand.
strings.追的人要穿过还在冒烟的瓦砾区: Whoever goes has to cross the still-smoking rubble
strings.逃到山上来的镇民，大多是老人。要吃要喝要地方睡，组织起来也能帮忙干活。: Townspeople who fled up the hill, most of them old. They need food, water and somewhere to sleep—and once organized, they can help with the work.
strings.逆火顺着坡往下烧，和往上爬的火撞在一起，“轰”的一声，两股火都矮了下去。: The backfire burns down the slope and meets the fire climbing up; with a roar, both sink low.
strings.通信公司的基站工程师: Base-station engineer at a telecom company
strings.遗物里的手机屏幕碎了。研究所的人花了两个月才把数据救回来：一分十二秒，海水退到了: The phone among the effects had a shattered screen. The institute took two months to recover the data: one minute twelve seconds of the sea drawing back past the harbour, and at the end a hoarse “Run!” The video went into the tsunami archive, with {actor}’s name under the title.
strings.避难的人里开始有人上吐下泻，接着是发烧。几十个人挤在一起，共用一个水桶、一个厕所: Among the evacuees, people start vomiting and having diarrhoea, then running fevers. With dozens of people crammed together, sharing one water bucket and one latrine pit, the sickness will spread fast.
strings.那一夜，八幡神社烧成了几根黑柱子。天亮以后，所有人挤在后山的背风坡上，一个一个地: That night the Hachiman Shrine burned down to a few black pillars. After daybreak everyone huddled on the lee slope at the back of the hill, searching for people one by one, calling out names. Those who lived: {survivors}. Those who never made it down from the hill: {dead}. Later, people rebuilt the shrine hall on the ruins and set up a stone beside it bearing a single line: After the tsunami, the fire came too.
strings.那件事被说破以后，{actor} 在山上一直坐在离火最远的地方。后来 {acto: After it came out, {actor} sat in the spot farthest from the fire for the rest of the days on the hill. Later {actor} went to Shiomi’s temporary shopping street, found the woman who had run the kiosk and put the money on her counter. She pushed it back and said only, “You lived. That’s enough.”
strings.那件事，{actor} 当着所有人说了出来。美咲没能走下那座山。后来每年三月，{: {actor} told everyone what had happened. Misaki never made it down from that hill. Every March afterwards, {actor} went back to Shiomi and spent an afternoon sitting on the stone steps of the Hachiman Shrine, counting from the first step to the last.
strings.那天上午，推土机终于在瓦砾中间推出了一条路。活下来的人一个一个上了卡车：{sur: That morning a bulldozer finally pushed a road through the rubble. One by one the survivors climbed onto the trucks: {survivors}. Those who did not live to see this day: {dead}. As the trucks pulled out of Shiomi, people were still sifting through the rubble on both sides of the road, piece by piece. They were searching for their families, and they kept searching until summer.
strings.那段视频后来被防灾研究所收进了海啸档案，连同开头那将近一分钟。{actor} 坚: The video later went into the Disaster Prevention Institute’s tsunami archive, with that first minute and all. {actor} refused to cut a single second: “The people who come after us need to see how people freeze.” Years later it was shown in disaster-prevention lessons at schools all over, and every time, the hoarse “Run!” on the soundtrack made the classroom go suddenly quiet.
strings.那段视频没了。{actor} 偶尔还会梦见二楼的那扇窗：海退到了港口外面，渔船歪: The video was gone. Now and then {actor} still dreamed of that second-floor window: the sea drawn back past the harbour, boats tilted in the mud, someone saying “Look at that” right in {actor.his} ear. Afterwards {actor} would go out onto the balcony and stand there until dawn.
strings.酒下了肚，脸上一下子热了——可那是皮肤底下的血管张开了，热量反而散得更快。千代奶: The sake goes down and faces flush at once—but that is the blood vessels under the skin opening up, and the body loses heat even faster. Granny Chiyo watches and shakes her head.
strings.酒瓶在火堆边传了一圈。: The bottle goes once around the fire.
strings.釜石的孩子们就是这么做的：觉得不安全，就再往高处跑；可要在雪地里折腾半夜: It’s what the Kamaishi children did: if it doesn’t feel safe, go higher; but it means half a night floundering in the snow
strings.钟声一下一下地传下山去。山脚下的瓦砾里，几支手电的光开始往石阶这边移动。: Stroke by stroke, the bell carries down the hill. In the rubble at the foot of the hill, a few flashlight beams start moving toward the stone steps.
strings.钟声传不到那么远。{actor} 没有回来。: The bell doesn’t carry that far. {actor} doesn’t come back.
strings.锹和锯只有那么几把，你们轮着用。雪地里，山腰上慢慢露出了一道黄土。: There are only a few shovels and saws, so you take turns. A line of yellow earth slowly appears across the snowy hillside.
strings.镇上建筑公司的工人，地震时正在港口边修一家民宿的屋顶。海啸把整栋房子推出去两百多: A worker for a building firm in town, he was repairing the roof of a guesthouse by the harbour when the quake hit. The tsunami carried the whole house more than two hundred metres; he was pinned under a fallen beam with half his body in muddy water. His daughter is at university in Sendai.
strings.镇上的老人能多熬几夜；你们自己要在风口里硬扛: The town’s old people can last a few more nights; you will have to tough it out in the wind
strings.镇公所储备室里的一箱压缩饼干: A case of hardtack from the town hall storeroom
strings.镇公所和诊所的废墟: The ruins of the town hall and the clinic
strings.镇公所门口那辆公务车的电瓶: The battery out of the official car parked by the town hall door
strings.队伍翻过山梁的时候，雪又下了起来。抬担架的人换了一拨又一拨，有人在路上倒下，就再: As the column crossed the ridge, it began to snow again. Team after team took turns at the stretchers; some fell by the way and never got up. Those who walked into the inland town: {survivors}. Those who didn’t make it: {dead}. Studies later found that far more old people died on long evacuations that year than were killed by the radiation itself.
strings.防灾仓库分给你们的几包压缩饼干，加上大家口袋里的零食。: A few packs of hardtack from the emergency supply shed, plus the snacks in everyone’s pockets.
strings.防灾仓库里有一台町里配的无线电台，地震时从架子上摔了下来，天线断了，电池也没电了: The shed holds a radio set issued by the town. It fell off its shelf in the quake: the antenna is broken and the battery is dead. Fix the wiring and the antenna, hook it up to a car battery, and you can talk to the town disaster headquarters.
strings.防灾仓库里的一个急救箱：纱布、三角巾、消毒水、几片止痛药。: A first-aid box from the emergency supply shed: gauze, triangular bandages, disinfectant, a few painkillers.
strings.防灾地图上写着那里，镇上的老人和孩子都往那里去。可楼顶只有十二米高，浪要是更高…: That’s what the hazard map says, and the town’s old people and children are all heading there. But the roof is only twelve metres up, and if the wave is higher…
strings.阿部一口一口喝完了两升温水，过了一个多钟头，大家才把房梁撬开。: Abe drinks the two litres of warm water mouthful by mouthful; over an hour later, they pry the beam up.
strings.阿部先输上了液，液压顶杆撑开了房梁。他被抬上担架的时候，冲大家竖了一下大拇指。: Abe gets an IV drip first, then the hydraulic jack forces the beam up. As they lay him on the stretcher, he gives everyone a thumbs-up.
strings.阿部喝了一夜的水，天亮时，尿的颜色淡了一些。他哑着嗓子说：“我欠你们一顿酒。”: Abe drinks water all night, and by dawn his urine is a little lighter. He croaks, “I owe you all a drink.”
strings.阿部在医院做了一个月透析，肾慢慢缓了过来，腿也保住了，只是走路一瘸一拐。第二年春: Abe spent a month on dialysis, his kidneys slowly recovered and he kept his legs, though he walked with a limp. The next spring he came back to Shiomi and helped build new houses on the high ground. On a beam in every house he built, he carved the same small line: “This one will never pin anyone.”
strings.阿部没能等到出去喝酒的那一天。他女儿后来读了研究生，研究的是海啸里木结构房屋的倒: Abe never got to go out for that drink. His daughter went on to graduate school and studied how wooden houses collapse in tsunamis. The acknowledgements of her thesis were a single line: “For my father, who waited a long time under a beam.”
strings.阿部熬过了那一夜。早上他睁开眼，第一句话是：“还活着？”: Abe makes it through the night. When he opens his eyes in the morning, the first thing he says is, “Still alive?”
strings.阿部的两条小腿没保住。装上假肢以后，他回了建筑公司，在高台上的工地当监工。女儿毕: Abe lost both lower legs. After he got prostheses he went back to the building firm as a site supervisor up on the high ground. The year his daughter graduated, she designed a tsunami-proof community hall; on the day construction began he stood at the very back of the crowd on his crutches and told no one.
strings.阿部被房梁压住的小时数。: How many hours Abe has been pinned under the beam.
strings.阿部被抬上了大巴。: Abe is carried onto the bus.
strings.阿部被抬上山以后，一开始还能开玩笑。几个钟头后，他突然说心口发慌、手脚发麻，脉搏: Once Abe is carried up the hill, he can even joke at first. A few hours later he suddenly says his chest is fluttering and his hands and feet are numb; his pulse races and slows, and his urine is the colour of soy sauce—crush syndrome.
strings.阿部被自卫队员用担架抬下了山。: The SDF troops carry Abe down the hill on a stretcher.
strings.陪他去的人要在黑夜里穿过火场边的瓦砾: Whoever goes with him has to cross the rubble beside the fires in the dark
strings.陪她下去找厂长的家: Go down with her to look for the manager’s house
strings.陪她坐一会儿，什么也不说: Sit with her a while and say nothing
strings.隔壁“潮风之家”养老院的老人，两年前摔断了髋骨，从此坐上了轮椅。年轻时是镇上的接: A resident of Shiokaze House, the nursing home next door. Two years ago she broke her hip and has been in a wheelchair ever since. In her younger days she was the town midwife and delivered half of Shiomi’s middle-aged people. This afternoon the home brought a few residents to the training centre for a joint drill, and Chiba, a caregiver, was pushing her chair.
strings.雨夹着雪，打在脸上像碎玻璃。在外面待几分钟就会湿透。: Rain mixed with snow stings the face like broken glass. A few minutes outside and you are soaked through.
strings.雨夹雪从屋檐和破了的窗户里灌进来，地上积起了泥水。所有人的衣服都湿透了。: Sleet pours in under the eaves and through the broken windows, and the floor turns to slush. Everyone is soaked through.
strings.雪夜里干重活，又冷又累，离火也最近；可防火带开得越早越管用: Heavy work on a snowy night, cold and exhausting and closest to the fire; but the earlier the firebreak is cut, the more good it does
strings.雪片又大又密，落在瓦砾上就化成了泥水。远处的火光在雪里一片模糊。: Big, thick flakes turn to slush as soon as they hit the rubble. The distant firelight is a blur in the snow.
strings.雪确实能压住火；可要是风再大一点……: Snow does damp the fire down; but if the wind picks up a little more…
strings.雪落在神社前的空地上，SOS 的大字被盖住了一大半。: Snow settles on the open ground in front of the shrine, burying most of the giant SOS.
strings.雪这么大，火上不来。别折腾，保存体力: With this much snow the fire won’t get up here. Don’t wear yourselves out—save your strength
strings.顺手拖回来的几块还算干的门板: A few fairly dry doors dragged back on the way
strings.顺着后山运木材的林道往上走，探明哪里塌了、哪里还能过人。认路的人去最合适。雪没化: Follow the logging road up behind the hill and find out where it has collapsed and where people can still get through. It’s a job for whoever knows how to find their way. The snow hasn’t melted, and it is colder in the mountains than on the hilltop.
strings.顺着震断的竹管往后山找，把断开的地方一节一节接上。要在冰冷的山沟里蹚水干活。接通: Follow the broken bamboo pipe up behind the hill and join the snapped sections back together, working knee-deep in an icy gully. Once it’s connected, the purification fountain will have clean spring water every day.
strings.领事馆的年轻人愣了一下，点点头：“行，抬上来。”: The young man from the consulate hesitates, then nods. “All right. Carry them on.”
strings.风一转，逆火反扑了回来，{actor} 的脸和手被燎起了一片水泡。: The wind shifts and the backfire turns back on them; {actor}’s face and hands come up in blisters.
strings.饮水机下面没摔破的几桶水: A few jugs of water under the water cooler, unbroken
strings.马上就能暖和；可门窗紧闭的屋子里烧煤油……: Warm right away, but burning kerosene in a sealed room…
strings.马上往山上跑：各自跑，谁也别等（津波てんでんこ）: Run for the hill now: everyone for themselves, wait for no one (tsunami tendenko)
strings.马上打给灾害对策本部：报山上的人数和伤员: Call the disaster headquarters now: report how many are on the hill and who is hurt
strings.马上撬开房梁，把他拖出来: Pry up the beam right now and drag him out
strings.马上派人去诊所的废墟找抗生素: Send someone to the clinic ruins for antibiotics now
strings.黑夜里蹚冰冷的海水；去晚了，那盏手电可能就灭了: Wading through icy seawater in the dark; wait too long and that flashlight may go out
strings.黑暗里，{actor} 一脚踩空，从半塌的屋顶上滚了下去。: In the dark, {actor} steps into nothing and tumbles off a half-collapsed roof.
strings.（小太郎一直望着港口的方向，耳朵一动不动。）: (Kotaro keeps staring toward the harbour, ears perfectly still.)
strings.（小太郎把一只湿手套叼到火边，又跑开了。）: (Kotaro carries a wet glove over to the fire, then trots away.)
strings.（小太郎挨着最小的那个孩子蹲下，任她把冻红的手塞进自己的毛里。）: (Kotaro settles next to the youngest child and lets her push her frozen red hands into his fur.)
strings.（小太郎突然站起来，冲着山下的黑暗低低地吼了一声。）: (Kotaro suddenly stands and gives a low growl at the darkness below the hill.)
strings.（小太郎蜷在渡边老人的脚边，鼻子埋进了尾巴里。）: (Kotaro curls up at Watanabe’s feet, nose buried in his tail.)
